name: Ted Cruz
subject: Will you read this short passage with me?
body:
This is life and death
| | | | |
---
Friend,
This message may be a bit different from what you’re used to, but frankly, it’s quite personal and important.
I'd like you to read this passage with me from Hebrews 13:3:
_"Continue to remember those in prison as if you were together with them in prison, and those who are mistreated as if you yourselves were suffering."__
_**__As a follower of Christ, nothing weighs heavier on my heart than the suffering of our brothers and sisters who are paying the ultimate price for their faith.**
I've seen the reports, heard the stories personally, and fought in the U.S. Senate to shine a light on this darkness because their pain is real, raw, and relentless.
They aren't distant statistics – _they're our family in Christ._
_Since 2009 in Nigeria, it's estimated that**over 100,000 Christians have been massacred, 20,000 churches have been destroyed** , and **over 5 million have been displaced.**_
_In China, it is not uncommon for faithful believers to be**arrested simply for gathering to worship** , to have their **homes raided** , and their **leaders imprisoned**._
_In Sudan, Islamist paramilitaries have long been on a rampage –**bombing churches** , and **killing priests and worshippers** sheltering inside while forcing survivors to **convert or be killed**. In some cases, crucified._
**Many don't realize it, but Christians are the most persecuted religious group on the planet, facing torture, rape, enslavement, and murder. At least 380 million endure heavy persecution – 60% of them children, with girls and women suffering the most violation.**
My faith demands I act, illustrated quite clearly in the verse I shared above, and I'd like to personally – _and urgently_ – ask you to do so as well.
**Save The Persecuted Christians is a vital non-profit organization engaged in this fight on the front lines by raising awareness, providing a megaphone to survivors, briefing lawmakers and government officials, and pushing relentlessly for real policy changes and accountability.**

We cannot stand idly by while evil targets the faithful. It's time to rally around our persecuted family, to show them they are not forgotten, that their American brothers and sisters stand with them in prayer and action.

Tina for Oregon [https://nvlupin.blob.core.windows.net/images/van/NGP/NGP12/1/92654/images/TinaForOregon-Logo-FullColor-white.png]
Peter,

This weekend, the Trump administration once again singled out Oregon - escalating fear and division instead of supporting the safety and rights of our communities.

In response, Governor Kotek joined Eugene-Springfield leaders to unite in support of peaceful protest and to make clear that Oregon will not be intimidated by reckless federal overreach.

As the Governor shared:

“I stand with Eugene-Springfield leaders in uplifting our values of peaceful protest. I share the outrage Oregonians are feeling about the Trump administration’s aggressive tactics that are provoking fear, tearing families apart, and making our communities less safe. As Governor, I stand in opposition to those actions, and I want immigrants, refugees, and communities of color to know that I will do everything I can to protect them.

“Indiscriminate and unlawful uses of crowd control tools by federal agents must stop. Whether in Eugene or Portland, or in any city in Oregon, a federal presence that meets the public with unnecessary force is fundamentally unacceptable in our nation.”

— Team Tina

| | Team, Senate Republicans are caving to Trump and preparing to pass a bill that could block tens of millions of eligible Americans from voting. **[And before we get into the details of just how harmful this bill could be, we need to ask if you can help us take action. Contact your Senator today and tell them to vote NO on the SAVE Act.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124812732/599797043/-984452826?refcode=emm_ffa_20260205_T1_SAVEActMobilization_v1s2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDMvMS84ODQ1MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyZDI2OThiYi1mMjAyLWYxMTEtODMyZi0wMDBkM2ExZjBlNGMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=BsvpknRFGF94l_qWdRu7Ym_xnBfyYD3oW5mntP9l9QE=&emci=e1db664d-f202-f111-832f-000d3a1f0e4c&emdi=2d2698bb-f202-f111-832f-000d3a1f0e4c&ceid=1037277)** The SAVE Act is a modern-day poll tax and a massive voter suppression bill that would require showing expensive government documents in person to register to vote — documents that 21 million American citizens don’t have easy access to. The bill also opens the door to harmful voter purges and could inevitably remove American citizens who have the right to vote from voter rolls. | [SAY NO to the SAVE ACT](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124812733/599797044/-984452826?refcode=emm_ffa_20260205_T1_SAVEActMobilization_v1s2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDMvMS84ODQ1MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyZDI2OThiYi1mMjAyLWYxMTEtODMyZi0wMDBkM2ExZjBlNGMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=BsvpknRFGF94l_qWdRu7Ym_xnBfyYD3oW5mntP9l9QE=&emci=e1db664d-f202-f111-832f-000d3a1f0e4c&emdi=2d2698bb-f202-f111-832f-000d3a1f0e4c&ceid=1037277)
---
The bill is so unprecedented that Republican Senators are discussing changing the filibuster — a decades-old Senate rule that requires 60 votes for a bill to pass — just to move it forward.

| | It has been over a month since the Affordable Care Act's enhanced premium tax credits expired. Those credits helped working families, seniors, and small business owners afford health insurance. **And we're already seeing the consequences of Trump and Republicans letting them lapse.** Premiums are spiking. Families are being forced to choose between paying more each month or dropping coverage altogether. **And new data shows ACA enrollment has fallen by more than one million people, with many more folks expected to drop coverage as the months go on.** [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124813121/599804023/945825667?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDEvMS84OTMyNSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiNjg1MDU2YS1mNDAyLWYxMTEtODMyZi0wMDBkM2ExZjBlNGMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=M0ihS3D5Z1H3iwtjgY1nNb0zyawD_Sv7I-SExS6G0wQ=&emci=ba599d1b-d102-f111-832f-000d3a1f0e4c&emdi=b685056a-f402-f111-832f-000d3a1f0e4c&ceid=7731215) For years, the enhanced tax credits made the ACA work the way it was intended to work: lowering costs, expanding coverage, and giving people the security of reliable health care. Peter,
Before I ran for the U.S. Senate, I was an investigative journalist leading a team that exposed corruption and human rights abuses worldwide.
This report in _The New York Times_ reminded me of what I saw in many of those investigations:

More and more, the atmosphere under Trump reminds me of countries where dissent is silenced by intimidation.
From the article:
_Fired federal workers who are worried about losing their homes ask not to be quoted by name. University presidents fearing that millions of dollars in federal funding could disappear are holding their fire. Chief executives alarmed by tariffs that could hurt their businesses are on mute. ..._
_“When you see important societal actors — be it university presidents, media outlets, C.E.O.s, mayors, governors — changing their behavior in order to avoid the wrath of the government, that’s a sign that we’ve crossed the line into some form of authoritarianism,” said Steven Levitsky, a professor of government at Harvard and the co-author of the influential 2018 book “How Democracies Die.”_
**This is unacceptable in the United States of America.**
Peter — As Trump dismantles checks on his power and purges the government to fill every office with loyalists, more and more Americans are too afraid of retaliation to speak up.
**This descent into an un-American America must be stopped. We must regain Congressional power.**

That means I’m MAGA’s #1 target for defeat.
**Help me beat them again, just like we did in 2021.**

| | | Team, it's Mark.

Most of you probably know that I am suing the Secretary of Defense. On Tuesday, I was in court to make my case against Pete Hegseth.

After 25 years in uniform and another 5 in the United States Senate, I never imagined I'd have to do something like that. Hegseth has left me no choice.

When he censured me and threatened my rank and retirement, he came after what I earned over 25 years — and chilled the free speech rights of every retired member of the military alongside me.

If Hegseth isn't stopped, our longest-serving military veterans will have to live with the constant threat that they could be deprived of their rank and pension years — even decades — after they leave the military if they say something he doesn't like.

I'm not going to sit by and let that happen. So, I sued Hegseth. And now, we wait and see what the court decides.

I've been truly humbled by the support people have sent my way over the past couple of months. It means the world to me that so many of you care about what Trump and Hegseth are trying to do.

That's how we've made it this far, and it's how we'll get to the other side of this chapter in our nation's history. Together.

Our neighbors in Minneapolis are suffering from ICE abuse and violence that the Supreme Court helped unleash. | |

Peter, **ICE’s ongoing violence and terror campaign is the direct result of the lawlessness the Supreme Court has unleashed in their mission to bow to a wannabe dictator.** Last September 2025, the Court blessed ICE’s horrifying raids in our communities, and gave the agency permission to racially profile people. **The Supreme Court’s disregard for justice has created turmoil for our neighbors in Minneapolis, some who have been unable to work since ICE descended, leaving them unable to pay rent.** As United for Democracy fights hard for needed, vital court reform, we’re also committed to supporting the on-the-ground work our allies are doing in communities right now to support the people. [**Take a moment to read Chelsie’s note below, and chip in a donation split between United for Democracy and the Minneapolis Regional Labor Federation’s rent fund.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqvd8hCserj-XmGYLB0-0IMX1om1J0_1aEV2b-kAgyJHHsXtq8k5iY8bvzDBsWY97Upla4jHhuvWYriDS1RB8_MtpD4M08InuI9894e2Joc-Td4w7OQUVLgSgrBPFykhacqQh0Cq8j1nh4AcdAALfG-6c9w88e-A3rJpa5jRExw3VZXlhlzGS-fvTMjIeduF0oFpC9IVrXhoEZsu6BYGL2rX9EsaKkOUarc5VdTbws9KgU_ns2PudjeUyuUWXKHnFu-VwcYwOYc4VBjI8FczNmZW4mrYgpgWz-SDbmoF8hRncs-8oXP34docxwbzy2WHPulrciQ_IXTN_ijB4HxwuClYHTIBZ1ZeunV2sD60Nbjlcg/4nx/hChLfpPeSUWYp1CRnlQ6LQ/h0/h001.OvjQTFXM-ZmlWCcVTBizazGPCLjqbBq_n3bh_FRktEg) Thank you, Stasha Rhodes
United for Democracy **– Chelsie’s note –** Peter, I’m the president of Minneapolis Regional Labor Federation, and my city is under occupation by the federal government. During this crisis, our community has pulled together, blowing whistles, following ICE vehicles, and doing everything we can to protect our neighbors from being kidnapped and detained by ICE and border patrol. **February is here, and the rent is due.** And that’s a problem for our neighbors. **Imagine this happening to you:** One of our members was detained by ICE in the parking lot of their workplace, where they were swept away to a facility in Texas. After two weeks in detention under astonishing conditions, being pressured to sign “voluntary” deportation orders, the worker was finally granted habeas and was released. Two other children in the household also work at the workplace where the detainment took place. It is not safe to return to work―so they have had no income for weeks. They are thankful to be reunited, but afraid that eviction is around the corner. **There are more stories like this than you can believe. These are the families we are supporting with rent.** [**Minneapolis Regional Labor Federation created a fund to pay the rent for families who can’t go to work because they are threatened by ICE. Our movement is built on the combined strength of $5 and $10 donations. When everyone gives a little, they go a long way. Can you split a donation to protect our neighbors?**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqvd8hCserj-XmGYLB0-0IMX1om1J0_1aEV2b-kAgyJHHsXtq8k5iY8bvzDBsWY97Upla4jHhuvWYriDS1RB8_MtLicG6xFpKAmgtHHvYecDOey7nKOrAYSZUq9s43P1MRJYdSbvBprla8knZNOGIoafzJqRD75OISwtyQtdpXjSKTSPCo5N5QlLkDuUhRkgyntd-oQ7Nhy0wL1Z65EvuFFV_JGoE1EOhlKwQaIL_X9VNXxOOeB-ndSQwHxZUi0WuHtqxiFaURpZylf34X9u2xYJiCb2PND7SOGtPDH1oggx6WA6n6Egxddg52GzsBzGIQG4soySg0xAUzRPNPdNv2HeZt8xG0bZnkZL5dnGCU_bYA/4nx/hChLfpPeSUWYp1CRnlQ6LQ/h1/h001._WacOKUG25-WacpxMC2BF7ybENbvkQEobiCS7Q_xZg8) One thing I’ve learned in this process is that it’s _difficult_ to pay someone else’s rent. We’ve called for an eviction pause during this emergency, but the government moves slowly and the crisis is now. **If we don’t hit our goals:** Landlords will begin eviction proceedings, potentially bringing law enforcement to the people who have successfully avoided ICE during the occupation. ####

|

# “Caltrain will connect all the Super Bowl activities this week from north to south and is the safest, greenest way to travel the Peninsula in comfort.”
# **\- Supervisor David Canepa**
---
| | | | **2026 February e-newsletter** **Battle brews over illegal fence blocking access to Thornton State Beach** Dear friends, I’m standing with our community to protect public access to Thornton State Beach in Daly City, a coastline that belongs to everyone because over the past three weeks, an 8-foot chain-link fence was erected on private land that blocks the only public access trail down to the beach. Even more alarming, a hand-drawn sign warning trespassers they would be shot was posted on the fence. This situation raises serious safety concerns and I’m urging the California Coastal Commission to step in, oppose these restrictions and require the removal of the fence to restore lawful public access to Thornton State Beach. The California Coastal Act clearly states private landowners cannot block public access to the sea. Our beaches are public resources and I will continue to fight to keep them open and accessible for all. There is only one trail down to the beach from Olympic Way in Daly City. This multi-use trail is a popular destination for recreation extending from the scenic bluffs and cliffs overlooking Thornton State Beach all the way down to the water. As a nearby resident, I routinely hike down to the beach from the parking area at the end of Thornton Beach Loop but the chain link fence currently restricts trail access to the beach. I’m confident the fence will be removed soon and access restored to the beach but until it is, I urge all visitors to the park to remain vigilant.
**Sacred Heart Prep, Daly City team up to renovate Marchbank Park Field** I was proud to join Sacred Heart Cathedral President Melinda Skrade, John Vigo and the entire SHC team recently at the groundbreaking for the historic renovation of Marchbank Park Field in Daly City. Together with Daly City Mayor Glenn Sylvester, Vice Mayor Teresa Proaño, Councilman Rod Daus-Magbual, Councilwoman Juslyn Manalo, City Manager Tom Piccolotti and the Daly City community they are providing a truly world-class facility for Daly City residents that will serve generations to come. Seeing this vision take shape is something our entire community can celebrate. This is a public-private partnership between Sacred Heart Cathedral Preparatory and Daly City to renovate the existing Marchbank Field which is underutilized. The project includes new replacement artificial turf, batting cages, improved bleachers for spectators, and facilities that will support multiple sports, as well as new sub-drainage system, field lighting, perimeter fencing and retaining walls. Seeing this vision take shape is something our entire community can celebrate. It reflects our shared commitment to youth opportunity, community pride, and healthy, active spaces where families and students can gather, play and build memories. I can’t wait to see the finished field and all the future generations who will benefit from this investment in our community, from athletes to families who simply want a place to play, connect and thrive. **It was a privilege to fight for public transit while serving on the MTC** After five meaningful years, I have stepped down from my role as a Commissioner with the Metropolitan Transportation Commission, and I’m grateful for the opportunity to have represented San Mateo County and our Board of Supervisors at the regional level. I was humbled to receive an honorary resolution by the Commission for my role as Chair of the Joint MTC ABAG Legislation Committee which played a pivotal role in the achievement of MTC’s top priority for the 2025 state legislative session by guiding development of the Connect Bay Area Act introduced as Senate Bill 63 by senators Scott Wiener and Jesse Arreguín. I was commended for continually urging a focus on improving the transit rider experience and helping to navigate its passage through the hearings-and-amendments process and floor votes in both the Senate and Assembly before the bill was signed into law by Gov. Gavin Newsom. From supporting Caltrain electrification and BART improvements in San Mateo County to expanding Bay Wheels in Daly City and advancing key regional upgrades, I worked to balance strong regional leadership with local advocacy. As I step away from MTC, I remain fully committed to serving our community, fighting for affordability, sustainability, opportunity and continuing this work both as a supervisor and a father. **M.P. Brown students get a lesson in civil liberties at 500 County Center** I had the honor of welcoming students from Margaret Pauline Brown Elementary recently to 500 County Center as we recognized Fred Korematsu Day of Civil Liberties and the Constitution. Seeing these young students from Daly City engage with this history right here in our halls of government is a powerful reminder of why Korematsu Day matters. Fred Korematsu stood up for his rights at a time when doing so came at great personal cost, and his courage ultimately helped expose a grave injustice and advance civil rights for generations to come. Korematsu Day is about more than remembering the past; it’s about teaching our kids the importance of speaking up, defending our Constitution, and standing against injustice wherever it appears. I’m grateful to our County Office of Education, the Court Community Outreach Committee and all our partners for creating meaningful, hands-on learning experiences that inspire students to become informed, engaged advocates for justice and equality. The future is brighter when our young people understand the power of their voices. **USF grad students look toward a future of public service** It was exciting to be back on the Hilltop at the beautiful University of San Francisco campus Tuesday night, Feb. 3, to sit down and engage in a lively discussion with my former Politics Professor Patrick Murphy, far left in the photo, and many of his current graduate students interested in pursuing a life of public service just as I’ve done since the day I graduated USF in 1998. Murphy is the faculty director for both the Masters of Urban and Public Affairs and Masters of Public Administration programs at USF and has inspired three decades of students to become future leaders. I shared a little about what a “day in the life” looks like serving on the San Mateo County Board of Supervisors this past 10 years, the choices and tradeoffs I’ve made along the way and what I’ve learned about persistence, public service and staying grounded in your values.

I’m always inspired by how thoughtful and engaged these students are. Their questions about leadership, decision-making and navigating public service in today’s challenging climate reminded me why it’s so important to invest in the next generation. Huge thanks Professor Murphy for the invitation and to the students for the energy and great conversation. I left encouraged about the future of public service. Go Dons!

**Interns wanted to join our team ** We are looking to add to our great group of interns we are currently working with. If you or someone you know may be interested in applying to my Internship Program, submitting this form is the first step: [https://forms.gle/hiKqtn7Rird5vXwB9](https://davidcanepa.us1.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c7592558e548bc8cc150aa5&id=873ffc4fe7&e=c0babbc643 "https://forms.gle/hiKqtn7Rird5vXwB9?fbclid=IwAR3YFH0mH828rtAUru5EFOO9GsMCasQYe1N7AUrmwAwBf30JTtXOSeCzKjs"). You can also reach out to Mike Richardson on my staff directly with any questions at [mrichardson@smcgov.org](mailto:mrichardson@smcgov.org "mailto:mrichardson@smcgov.org"). In friendship,
**DAVID J. CANEPA**
President, San Mateo County Board of Supervisors

USF grad students look toward a future of public service It was exciting to be back on the Hilltop at the beautiful University of San Francisco campus Tuesday night, Feb. 3, to sit down and engage in a lively discussion with my former Politics Professor Patrick Murphy, far left in the photo, and many of his current graduate students interested in pursuing a life of public service just as I’ve done since the day I graduated USF in 1998. Murphy is the faculty director for both the Masters of Urban and Public Affairs and Masters of Public Administration programs at USF and has inspired three decades of students to become future leaders. I shared a little about what a “day in the life” looks like serving on the San Mateo County Board of Supervisors this past 10 years, the choices and tradeoffs I’ve made along the way and what I’ve learned about persistence, public service and staying grounded in your values. I’m always inspired by how thoughtful and engaged these students are. Their questions about leadership, decision-making and navigating public service in today’s challenging climate reminded me why it’s so important to invest in the next generation. Huge thanks Professor Murphy for the invitation and to the students for the energy and great conversation. I left encouraged about the future of public service. Go Dons! President Trump just crossed a line.
He’s now openly calling for Republicans to take over over elections by “nationalizing” them — stripping states of their authority and handing personal control over to a president who already tried to bully, pressure, and lie his way into staying in power.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=260205em-rs [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=260205em-rs]

We’ve already stopped Trump’s illegal efforts twice in court. We blocked attempts to pry into Oregon’s private voter data. We defended state elections and Oregon’s gold-standard vote-by-mail system. We won, and we’re prepared to do it again.
But make no mistake: these fights are deliberate, ongoing, and relentless. Trump and his allies are counting on states backing down. I won’t — and I know you won’t either.

Join me in the fight today, and let’s get to work. >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=260205em-rs]

Tobias Read

| | | | | | When a county DA goes on national TV threatening to arrest federal agents, someone who's actually been inside a federal courtroom needs to set the record straight. [This week, former federal prosecutor Reeve Swainston did exactly that.](https://nodoubtaboutitpodcast.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=d2649c77b4f4f1f9d512804d2&id=e63b8efc1a&e=567664f14c)

---](https://nodoubtaboutitpodcast.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=d2649c77b4f4f1f9d512804d2&id=0096908075&e=567664f14c)
| |
🔥 **FORMER PROSECUTOR DISMANTLES DA BREGMAN'S ICE THREATS**
Swainston wrote a blistering Albuquerque Journal op-ed. Then he came on our show to go deeper.
There's a specific federal statute — Title 8 USC 1357 — that Bregman is either ignoring or doesn't understand.
Swainston breaks it down in plain English. When you hear what the law actually says, you'll understand why Bregman's threats are legally meaningless — and why they're dangerous.

🚨 **"COMPLIANCE SAVES LIVES"**
New video shows Alex Pretti spitting on ICE agents and kicking their vehicle in Minneapolis. He had a gun on him. Faced zero consequences.
Ten days later, he was dead.
Swainston's argument: If Minneapolis had arrested him that day, he'd likely still be alive.

---
| |

🍋 **DON LEMON CHARGED UNDER FACE ACT
** Don Lemon invaded a church in St. Paul with protesters. Now he's facing federal charges. But that's not even the most embarrassing part. We play you the legendary clip where Lemon claims "a misdemeanor is not a crime" on the streets of Chicago — and a random couple completely owns him on camera.

📚 **TEACHER UNIONS HANDING OUT "HOW TO FIGHT ICE" PAMPHLETS**
You have to see this to believe it. Instruction manuals — distributed to students — that literally acknowledge "some of these acts may constitute a crime." Who's funding this? Swainston has thoughts.

👮 **THE 55 GANGS VIDEO**
A candidate for mayor in Long Beach posted a video calling all 55 gangs to meet him at City Hall. His goal? Fight federal law enforcement.

For sure."_ While Democrats are trying to walk that comment back, the rest of us know the truth when we hear it. They don't want to be on the ballot with their own unpopular tax increase.Oregonians played by the rules. They organized, gathered signatures, and demanded a say. Changing the election date after the fact sends a clear message: voter input is welcome only when it's convenient for those in power.This isn't about whether you support or oppose the gas tax. What I hear over and over again is frustration with insider maneuvering and procedural games that leave families paying more while accountability disappears.That's why I'm running to be your Republican nominee for governor.Oregon needs executive leadership that respects voters, owns decisions, and doesn't hide from tough questions. We need leaders who are willing to face the public honestly, not move the goalposts when things get uncomfortable.If you believe Oregon deserves transparency, accountability, and leadership that shows up, I hope you'll stay engaged and stand with me.--

Now, Donald Trump is back in the White House with unchecked power.
His ICE agents are terrorizing communities with masks and military weapons -- just like his insurrectionists did on January 6th. The only difference is that now they're being paid with your tax dollars.
His MAGA enablers in Congress are letting him treat the Constitution like it's optional. They're ignoring subpoenas. They're refusing oversight. They're acting like Trump is a king instead of a president.

Mississippi Republicans like to say elections are about choices. Last week, voters were given one more choice, though not at the ballot box. When Lt. Gov. Delbert Hosemann and Senate Education Chairman Dennis DeBar quietly killed school choice legislation, they forced an uncomfortable but necessary question: are they even Republicans anymore?
Gov. Tate Reeves didn't mince words. He said he had "never been more disappointed" in Hosemann and DeBar, accusing them of working with Democrats to kill a Republican priority "in the dark." He went further, calling the Senate Education Committee the place "where conservative priorities go to die" and where "the Democrat philosophy still dominates." Those are not throwaway lines. They are an indictment from the leader of Mississippi's Republican Party of its own Senate leadership.
And when you hold the Senate's actions up against the Mississippi GOP platform, the disconnect is impossible to ignore.
The Republican platform is explicit: education should be measured by results, not just spending. It prioritizes classroom instruction over bureaucracy, supports parental authority, and--most importantly--states plainly that parental involvement "should extend to allowing parents to choose the school that best meets the educational needs of their children." That is not ambiguous language. That is a direct endorsement of school choice.
Yet Hosemann and DeBar used their power to ensure parents never got that option. Not by winning an argument on the floor. Not by persuading a majority of legislators. But by stopping the bill cold in committee.
That approach mirrors the very education status quo Republicans have criticized for decades: centralized control, protection of entrenched interests, and an utter disregard for outcomes--especially for low-income families trapped in failing schools. Mississippi Republicans campaign against that model every election cycle. But when the moment came to act, the Senate leadership sided with it.
This isn't a disagreement over tactics or timing. It's a philosophical divide. The GOP platform emphasizes parental authority, competition, efficiency, and student-centered results. The Senate's decision protected administrative power and denied parents choice. One of those positions is Republican. The other simply isn't.
Party labels matter because they signal values. If Hosemann and DeBar no longer believe parents should choose schools, if they believe education decisions should be monopolized by government systems, and if they are comfortable partnering with Democrats to block conservative reforms behind closed doors, then honesty demands clarity.
No one is saying Democrats don't have a right to oppose school choice. They do. But Mississippi voters also have a right to know when their elected officials no longer align with the party they claim to represent.
Perhaps it's time for Hosemann and DeBar to make it official. If they reject the Republican Party's stated principles on education, parental authority, and reform, then changing parties would be more straightforward than continuing to campaign under a banner they no longer uphold.
At minimum, Mississippi Republicans deserve leaders who will fight for the platform they ran on--or step aside for those who will.

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. After Trump and MAGA Republicans cut funding for public broadcasting, NPR, PBS and many local stations face an existential threat that will hit local communities first and hardest.

**According to one estimate, 78 public radio stations and 37 TV stations were at risk of going dark as a result of the cuts.**

That means fewer local journalists, less emergency information, and fewer trusted sources of news — _especially in rural and underserved areas._

**This isn’t accidental. Trump wants to silence reporters who fact-check his lies and hold those in power accountable.**

We can’t let that happen. A free, independent press is essential to our democracy, and public pressure is one of the strongest tools we have to protect it.

## Winter Olympics Officially Open Today
The 2026 Winter Olympics Opening Ceremony kicks off today in Italy in the [most far-flung](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFuwyAURb8Gb1iAbZwMDF28pWtHC5ln8xpsELwG-e-rJOoXdD3D1bnn6zbfLAY8tk-7g6E1zgfUEoAI8hzDuSdcSkxw4LEVisu9rDaEWQmluVBc6NlZDOfcN86sAAq6BowcR9Fdxm4cGm-6VSyDFMKBvQy6s-4KVsleDdfFLXoRDZrnmlBCy15qObT9KNdhXIeLdNqB61kvwCHF3H5HPMjDGs74gNwucW-C8USpsO6DqYmpqdba3rf408a8MTWVFDMVpqa3seTyytREHvgL_D3kNgN_0j0W4hUdlJTBOo4H91go5pMXAF69pcK9Te8ivHrI0GTjUsUQsOiR9WLbLYaXHP2r6MOo3wAAAP__iRGLtw) Winter Games ever, with roughly 250 miles between Milan’s arenas and Cortina’s mountain venues. Tonight’s opening ceremony will take place at Milan’s San Siro Stadium, repurposed from a soccer venue to host the event. The musical extravaganza is expected to draw about [60,000 live spectators](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDGvpCAURn8NdhhEAS0otrGbbbc0KJfx7iAYIEP89y8zeVO8-tX35uR8599tuRn0GO5_zQG6uLgEqNlDKZCW6K_jxC3HEwKGey5xe2RnvF8445IyTplcrEF_LUNjtQPg0DegO6VYP6peiWbX0wRGSDd1vZJCSDBSjMzAODi7rnZdG9QvGuNMdkMnO9EOqnNCOTF2VlqwAxkYWCwxtf8jhrKD81d8Qmq3eDRe76WcmfR_CJ8Jn2utbVg36-rrTPj8GUH4_LY-0JtAt5gKBkP4nGAHk7LxtEAodIcEmdbdFHqYB-Sf_7RiKJDoB0q_09ANEhwxXDSfsKHxhM_9pLjiPeFzk7Q9K3qPWSoysPth0L_ty6-SPzX_CgAA___-fZjD). The live broadcast window runs 2-5 p.m. ET for U.S. viewers, putting all the pageantry right into the middle of the workday. [Here's how to watch](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD2u4yAURldjd1iAMTgFxTTuMu2U1jVcx8zwYwET5N0_JXpZwes_HZ3z_bmvd3DexcdvCKjrntaIrXisFfOa_BVOZ0o6Mbr4KDWZf2UH71dOuSSUEypXC85fq-it3hE5jj1qphQdZzWqqT_0jLfbJuQsgYmNWdhvjM5KyFGIbaYAvdMvGuVUMsEkmwah2D6pfZqZlRat6ARF62rKw9_kYj1w91d6Yh5MCr3XR61n6cZfHV86vrTWhriZj_pr0_HlFdXx5UiNNKjmIN9JxGDGkOJF3kXBeYjEpFxdBPJhkPokEC0pNSMEUsyB9r_HPmt7Nue9K1J1gj4COP92qj868qn5VwAAAP__2sKKYg). Americans have participated in every Winter Olympics since the very first in 1924, piling up [330 total medals](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOpDAQRL_GZCDbgM0EDi4hm0svRB7cHvq2bSPcGsTfr9hf2LhKVU_v33N5eiTM778-geNYlgxnJWCGYyl0pR3XWnbImN-Vy_pVoydatNSmlbqVZgke6VqGJrgIoKFvwClrZT_Z3o7N5qYJZDS9fU06BDX6x2vsvfUPpaLRoNYG3b0mtTRqUEaN3WBVHG0cJxVMgDCIQUJALkf3v2DmDSJd5QNHt5bUkNuY9yr6P0LPQs_neXZ8A4e6l4PrXRJ6hg9krneOmeEQek4QPLXsiS6hZ0_UMiboNk7N4cJ-IhFWY8Ug38kj_Zzxrwx9nP4OAAD__wqWfAc) and 114 gold ones over the last century. Team USA has found the podium in _almost_ every sport in the Winter Olympics (we’ve never won a medal in biathlon), but the Games this year added a brand-new event in ski mountaineering, an event no one has yet won. [Here's the full Olympics event schedule.](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0D2OpDAUBODTmAzkP2w6cLAJWW-6ITL2c_N2HjbCnkZ9-1GPNCeYvPRVqf7dl7tHwvz463dwLZUlw1UJWoNzKfTaDwy1HJAxP2or4aMmT7RILk3PZc_NEj3Sa9FddAlAgurACWu5mqyyY7c5lSy3ehI3w296tVEGAVFNIphVqXVcO3RvjUtuhBZGjIO2Io02jZOIJkLUTHOI2Mo5_C-Y2waJXuUJ5xDK3pHbWjsqU3-YnJmcr-safna_A0zOkJmcdySfSx_K2TD7_l3J5FzDBvGToDtdPC4kwmos0_yxe6Rvv_3qlKeTXwEAAP__-a515w)
## Stocks Slide as Tech and Bitcoin Fall
The [Dow Jones Industrial Average tumbled](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFuhDAQRL_GdCBjjE0KF2noLm1K5LN3D-cWjPDmEH8fcb-QZpqR3mje9226-URpfXz5BRxjnlY4CgEz7FOmc9lSKHmDNa2Pwjk8C3qiSUllaqlqaaboE52TrqJDAAVdBa61VnaD7WxfzU77uwl6QPzwaAepcUC0GpTWMWBobZXcRZNKmla3pu0bbVvsLfZDG02EqIWWEBPnvfnJaeUZkM78gr0JeanIzcxbEd2nUKNQ43EcTVjv4SqFGi-0UKNUV2ihxveJevH7E7jmHP1ZU3pB_btFz1CamReqdhe3IxGlYqzQ8rH4RO81_peil1N_AQAA__-zXXqR) Thursday as a sharp sell-off in big tech rattled Wall Street, with Amazon plunging 10% in after-hours trading after it estimated roughly $200 billion in future spending. The tech-heavy [Nasdaq took the brunt](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2SnDAQBOCngWwo_SHtBgROyM6pQ0onjZbxDRJGYrd4e9feK1ze1dVf__lYPjwx5cdvv-HUUlkyvipja3gsha9tp1DLjpnyo7YSvmryzIsSyoJQIOwSPfG1mD5OCVGh7nGSzgl9c9qN_ToJLaWN5i6SFcYEfTNaeGu19tK6cFc9Te82oYSVRlo5DsbJNLo03mS0EaPpjMBIrRzD30K5rZj4Kk88hlC2nqe1tb12-len5k7NibLPAYfLr6W8E52a36ROzUxP7NT8zYDNH1_YoJXoL4jlBXWHUQjIvkb_DyoyQ0kJPk_iWMFXaBhWOMrZIJTcKJ9Y4ZNaKJRh5zM_sIKSQsi7c-Owto37Y4r7i5ipWtcZ8dg88ffq9qOrn5P6HwAA___sPpPm) of the damage, dragged down by fears that massive artificial intelligence investments are pushing profitability out further than investors expected. Bitcoin slid about 13%, falling [below $64,000 for the first time](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGOtCAUBeCnwU5zQQSnoPgbu_nbLQ3CZby7CEbYMb79xn2FbU5zku8k5-M5Py1FSq__dkNTQ54TniVirXjMOV7bTq7kHROlV6nZfZVgY5wFCNWCaEHN3lK8Ztl4ExAF9g0arjX0o-710KxGLlJxPTq1gLI6WK4fGtXg-sco0fuhIXNrIEBxyRUfOql5GHQYRu6VRy-ZBPRU89F9Zkp1xRCv_Majc3lrollr3Qvr_zExMTGd59m5tLi7ZGK6aSYmEHcMTEwLVZcptftBDtuavb1aDQDQUmpDdt-lW-sWm8P4_aQYqSjNJLw2S_F3sP7ppbcRPwEAAP__0F95mA) since late 2024, as investors pulled back from riskier assets and doubts grew about crypto’s role as a safe haven. Analysts said heavy liquidations and institutional selling are accelerating the move, tying the cryptocurrency slump more tightly to the broader tech-led market rout.
## Car Insurance Costs Drop Nationally
Car insurance prices [fell 6% nationally](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkMFuhCAYhJ8GbxhARHvgsE3jbfe4PRoWfpQtggFWY5--sYe-QI-TyUxmvs_reFXOuzDd1AKy2DgG2LOHUiCN0R_L6nSOKwQXplyi_spWeT8ywgQmDBMxGuX8MfLKSAvAoKlA0q4jTd81XVvN0irdt5pRK95Ia6DpOWkfVjyEsUIDt5WTZxthRFBOBW1r3lHbdrbtqREGDEecgHElpvoZXSgzWH_EDVKt41J5OZeyZtRcEBsQG_Z9r5ccTg-xAQJ-ZcSGJQY4EBtcyK-kggbEBq0S_tM4qQIZqwT4POjChB-vgkMsGDZIxz5DOkMq4cuF3r-32xM1Q9TOoObj_eQHe75DWqskzbo7710WHeJkWpTzv0vLv_Bukv0EAAD__1FjkbA) in 2025 to an average of $2,144 for full coverage after surging 46% from 2022 to 2024, according to a new analysis. Some states saw [dramatic relief](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkMFurCAYhZ8GdxhAFF2wmJtbd9PltDvDyK_-LYIBHOPbN_YVujvJSU7O933ch7tBh35-NyvoPIXBw5Ec5AxxCO5cNxxT2MCjn1MO43eajHODYKKhTFDWDNagOwdZWD0BCKgK0FwpVrWqUnWx6M5IbhmvjepM17XWtFyqhlfSdJbXT1WgvtaYYA2XvOF1KRWfajXVLbeNBSuJZGAxh1h-BfR5gcmd4QWxHMNaOL3kvCVS3YjoieiP4yjX5K-OiB483RMR_QVFRL8FhxnHK44mUvRpj8aPQLcIK-5roiYCndAb5056kaKf6XPP1IdM4QXxPBaIQERvIr3d-OPtM1lS9WFES6r__y6RcKQHxK2I2m4HOoepUUSyeTXofi_nP3l-afETAAD__z0Ok_w) with Wyoming dropping 30%, Iowa falling 25% and Arkansas declining 23%. However, 10 states bucked the trend with New Jersey rising 20% and Washington, D.C., climbing 18% to become the nation's most expensive city for full-coverage insurance at an average of $4,017 annually. Analysts said insurers' improved financial margins now allow them to cut rates and compete for customers. The report projects a modest 1% national increase in 2026. See the [average annual car insurance cost by state here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L1u8yAUxvGrwVsiwHz4HRjexVu6dkSIc4hPi8ECmsh3XyW30PV5pN_w_7z5W6BM5f4RdnQjVV_w2TOOgc3XfO4HxV4PLFTufdT43VPI2UsuzYXLCzceAuXTqwlcQpQ4T-iEtXxe7Gz1tDkA0DGa8C-lOakk7MKB6yBsgmXWoCZyL41LboQSRuirsiJpm_QiwACCYooj0Kjt-lWpjA1TPusD2zXWfcpuG-PobP7P5MrkSqX_NErn62RyjaFd3lMoEZlcGx61DSbXqTk4npQzdWOZ4vc9UH6L408ZHk7-BgAA___LRHJo).

| Letter from the Chair
---
Why Bother Voting? Addressing the Common Excuses
If you're reading this newsletter, you're likely more engaged in politics than most. You're also probably more inclined to vote when election time rolls around.
Lately, I've been reflecting on the reasons people give for sitting out elections--and how we might thoughtfully respond when friends, family, or neighbors share them. These excuses come up often, especially among people of faith. Here's a closer look at a few, along with some perspective to consider.
"I'm Tired of Voting for the Lesser of Two Evils"
This is one of the most common frustrations: neither candidate feels inspiring, so why choose the "lesser evil"?
Father Chad Ripperger, a respected Catholic priest and theologian, offers a compelling moral framework here. He explains that when you vote in such a scenario, you're not endorsing evil--you're actively working to preserve the good that would be lost if the greater evil prevailed. Failing to act in that situation, allowing the worse outcome by default, can amount to negligence--a sin of omission.
This shifts the focus from "approving" a flawed choice to protecting what's valuable. It's a practical way to navigate imperfect options while staying true to conscience.
"It's in God's Hands--Why Vote at All?"
Some believers see voting as unnecessary because ultimate outcomes rest with God. And it's true: Scripture doesn't command voting, and in the U.S., it's a right, not a legal obligation. No one sins by abstaining purely on those grounds.
Yet faith traditions often highlight positive reasons to participate:
Voting can be an act of charity toward our neighbors--seeking policies that promote human dignity and the common good. It's an exercise in stewardship--using the civic gifts we've been given to help preserve them for future generations.
Of course, some faiths prohibit voting as a matter of conscience, and no one should pressure anyone to go against their deeply held beliefs. But for most people of faith, voting aligns with loving our neighbor and being responsible caretakers.
Imagine if all people of faith in Nebraska stayed home on Election Day. Our small towns, communities, and state policies would look very different--likely shifting in ways that could undermine the values that we hold dear.
"My Vote Doesn't Count Anyway"
With headlines about election irregularities, ballot issues, fraud claims, and more, it's easy to feel disillusioned. Skepticism is understandable.
But look at 2024: President Trump's "too big to rig" strategy--mobilizing massive turnout--demonstrated that winning big is still possible despite challenges. Nebraska and many other places lean strongly one way, yet turnout makes the difference.
Here's the hard truth: Your vote definitely won't count if you don't cast it. If every potential Republican voter showed up consistently, outcomes in Nebraska (and beyond) would be decisive victories.
The Reality of Commitment
Voting is a commitment, and like any commitment, it faces obstacles--bad weather, busy schedules, frustration, or apathy. Some voters are "fair-weather patriots," showing up only when it's convenient. Others vote faithfully every cycle. Most of us fall somewhere in between.
The key is recognizing that consistent participation matters more than perfection. Showing up, even when it's not ideal, is how we influence the direction of our communities and country.
Closing Summary
At its core, voting isn't about finding a flawless hero--it's about protecting the good, stewarding our rights, and loving our neighbors through the choices available to us.
In Nebraska and across the country, high turnout among engaged citizens--including people of faith--would shape outcomes that affect families, communities, and future generations. Your vote is one piece of that puzzle, but when combined with others, it's a catalyst for positive change.

Sincerely, Mary Jane Truemper Chairman, Nebraska Republican Party

Peter,

In less than two weeks, millions of people will gather to watch the biggest football game of the year. **Bright lights.**
**Packed hotels.** **Most people don't know this...** Wherever crowds gather, traffickers follow. Major sporting weekends bring increased travel, full hotels, busy airports, and distracted attention. **Behind the excitement ...**
**Children will go missing.** This is the perfect environment for exploitation. Law enforcement and child protection organizations know this pattern well. **Trafficking spikes around large events because vulnerability increases. **While millions are preparing for entertainment, vulnerable children are facing danger. They're not thinking about scores or highlights, but hoping to be safe - waiting for help before harm happens. This is why this moment matters. Here is a truth that should stop us cold: **9 out of 10 missing children are trafficked right here in the United States.** That's why I'm reaching out to you today. The**Sound of Freedom Foundation** exists to interrupt these moments of danger with protection, prevention, and action. We are not here for awareness alone.Awareness without action does not save a child. We are here to stop trafficking before it starts, support intervention efforts, and protect children when the risk is highest. **But this mission is not an idea. ****It is personal. **
**It is lived. **
**It is carried by those who know danger firsthand.**
---

My name is Theresa Flores. I'm a survivor of child trafficking. And today, I work to help protect children **before they disappear.** **I was fifteen years old. **
**An honor student. **
**A daughter. ** A girl who trusted the wrong "friend." **I was trafficked for two years.**

Most people imagine trafficking happens far away...in dark alleys...in other countries.

To "other people." **But that's not how it usually happens.** Right now, as set up for the big game is underway, **120 trained partner volunteers are already on the ground in the Bay Area**. Men and women working _this week_ --
Training hotel staff to recognize danger. Walking hotel halls, parking garages and public spaces. **Watching.**
**Reporting.**
**Protecting.** **Standing where traffickers don't expect resistance.** Children cannot choose safety on their own. They depend on adults to act when danger is highest. Freedom is not a word painted in an end zone. It's safety, dignity and the chance to grow up without fear. Your donation right now helps fund prevention programs, strengthen intervention efforts, and protect innocent lives from trafficking and abuse.It turns high-risk moments into moments of defense and hope.

**Pray for the ones who are afraid to speak.**
**Pray for courage, protection, and rescue.** Jesus said, _" Let the little children come to me... and do not hinder them."_ This is how we don't hinder them.

I was fifteen years old. An honor student. A daughter. A girl who trusted the wrong "friend." I was trafficked for two years. Most people imagine trafficking happens far away...in dark alleys...in other countries. To "other people." But that's not how it usually happens. Right now, as set up for the big game is underway, 120 trained partner volunteers are already on the ground in the Bay Area. Men and women working this week -- Training hotel staff to recognize danger. Walking hotel halls, parking garages and public spaces. Watching. Reporting. Protecting. Standing where traffickers don't expect resistance. Children cannot choose safety on their own. They depend on adults to act when danger is highest. Freedom is not a word painted in an end zone. It's safety, dignity and the chance to grow up without fear. Your donation right now helps fund prevention programs, strengthen intervention efforts, and protect innocent lives from trafficking and abuse.It turns high-risk moments into moments of defense and hope. The game will last a few hours. Your impact lasts a lifetime. Your generosity will create awareness and help ordinary people recognize danger before another child is harmed.While millions will be watching, traffickers will be working. But so will our partners. And with your help, we can be faster and more effective in protecting children who need us most. We will place 30,000 soap packets into hotel rooms--each one printed with a missing child hotline number. That number has saved lives. Because sometimes, the only moment a child is truly alone... is in the bathroom. This is what rescue looks like before a headline or a news story. Right now, I'm asking you to do something just as important as giving. Please pray that they'll be found. Pray for the children whose names we don't know yet. Pray for the ones who are afraid to speak. Pray for courage, protection, and rescue. Jesus said, " Let the little children come to me... and do not hinder them." This is how we don't hinder them. This is how we show up. This is your moment to step onto the field for freedom. This is your chance to make the play that changes a child's future. If you feel led to take the next step, here's how your gift helps protect children during this dangerous week: $60 helps equip one trained volunteer $120 strengthens outreach and training materials $180 expands protection across multiple hotel locations $240 multiplies our presence when traffickers are most active Traffickers are already preparing. But so are we. Because of people like you. Because of prayer. God 's children are not for sale. For God's Children, Theresa Flores Freedom Fighter For the Sound of Freedom Foundation 6671 Southwest Freeway, Suite 700, Houston TX 77074

name: Patrick J. Murphy
subject: From the Front with Patrick J. Murphy: Superbowl Sunday
body:
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP25/1/106220/images/PJM_Logo.png]
This Sunday, roughly half the country will stop what it’s doing and pay attention to the same thing at the same time. That alone makes the Super Bowl unusual in modern American life.
I’ve been 3 times before, including last year when the Eagles won. Go Birds!
I’m back again this year in Santa Clara, though not for the game itself. I’m here for everything that happens around it: the panels, the meetings, the sponsorships, the machinery that turns a football game into one of the largest economic events in America.
In my latest Substack [https://substack.com/home/post/p-186614172] I write about the Super Bowl economy and the paradox at its core: how a night that unites the country and generates extraordinary wealth often leaves behind many of the athletes whose labor and sacrifice make the spectacle possible once our attention moves on.
The average NFL career lasts just 3.3 years [https://runrepeat.com/nfl-player-career-length?utm_source=chatgpt.com] . Roughly 78% of former NFL players face financial difficulties. Almost every single player that played at a collegiate level and beyond experiences physical pain in their day to day lives. These men give their bodies to the game, each play like surviving a car crash, and many are left dealing with injuries, cognitive decline, and financial ruin.
Football players are true warriors, and not surprisingly, support for and from our military is deeply embedded throughout the night of the Big Game.
Every Super Bowl features flyovers, color guards, and “Salute to Service” patches stitched onto jerseys. Patriotism is woven seamlessly into the broadcast, including a live tv clip of overseas troops watching the game in uniform.
What’s less visible is the scale behind it.
The Department of Defense spends millions advertising around the Super Bowl, running recruitment campaigns aimed at the same young men who idolize NFL players. The Army [https://www.war.gov/News/Feature-Stories/Story/Article/3294082/defense-agency-ad-gets-super-bowl-slot-on-afn/] , Navy [https://news.usni.org/2023/02/13/navy-spent-about-1-8-million-on-super-bowl-ads] , and Marines [https://time.com/5539120/marine-corps-super-bowl-ad-hack/?utm_source=chatgpt.com] all buy Super Bowl ad space. The Navy alone spent $1.8 million on Super Bowl advertising in 2023.
Since 2011, the NFL has raised over $75 million [https://www.nfl.com/causes/salute/?utm_source=chatgpt.com] through its Salute to Service program for veteran charities like the Wounded Warrior Project, the USO, and the Pat Tillman Foundation.
But here's what the NFL doesn't talk about much: the players who actually served.
Pat Tillman walked away from a $3.6 million contract with the Arizona Cardinals after 9/11 to enlist in the Army Rangers with his brother Kevin. They served in Iraq and Afghanistan and Pat was killed by friendly fire in 2004. He was 27.
Roger Staubach won the Heisman Trophy, served a tour in Vietnam, then came home and won two Super Bowls with the Dallas Cowboys.
Rocky Bleier was shot in Vietnam and had part of his foot blown off by a grenade. Doctors said he'd never play again. He returned and won four Super Bowls with Pittsburgh.
West Point grad Alejandro Villanueva served three tours in Afghanistan as an Army Ranger, earned a Bronze Star, then became a Pro Bowl offensive tackle.
Several current active reserve troops currently play in the NFL, including Philadelphia Eagles backup guard Brett Toth, a West Point graduate. I helped change this policy to allow active reservists to play professional sports (NFL, WNBA, etc) with then-SASC Chairman John McCain when I was in the Pentagon.
These athletes are reminders that the same grit, discipline, and sacrifice we celebrate on the field Sunday night exist in people who served our country.
So enjoy the game. Enjoy the ads, the halftime show, and all the food. Just remember that these guys are putting their bodies on the line for our entertainment. Whether wearing a helmet on a football field or in a war zone, they’re showing up with the grit behind greatness.
That's worth celebrating, too.
- Patrick
Be sure to follow me on Instagram [https://www.instagram.com/patrickmurphypa/?hl=en] and subscribe to my Substack [https://substack.com/@patrickmurphypa] for my weekly geopolitical and business analysis .

Dear Friends and Alabamians,
Black History Month celebrates Alabama's profound civil rights legacy, from the marches that changed our nation to the resilient spirit of Black communities across our state. Today, the fight continues for economic empowerment in rural and urban areas alike, where poverty, disinvestment, and inequality have persisted too long. I've traveled our state, listening to families in places that have been left behind.
[| | | | | Kyle Sweetser

@kyleforalabama
Overflow event tonight in Evergreen, Alabama! The Conecuh County Democrats are back in force!
| 2:35 AM * Feb 3, 2026 * 1.2K Views2 Replies * 10 Reposts * 60 Likes

Across Alabama, Black communities boast rich histories but face common challenges: high unemployment, crumbling infrastructure, and limited access to opportunities. From revitalizing tourism tied to civil rights sites to fixing sanitation and expanding infrastructure in rural counties, we need bold investments.
As your Senator, I'll secure federal funds for infrastructure upgrades, job creation, and public-private partnerships that uplift communities statewide. By rejecting harmful policies and championing free markets, we can turn legacy into lasting growth.
It's time for government to invest in the people, protect constitutional rights, and ensure no corner of Alabama is left behind. Join our campaign. Together, we'll foster opportunity FOR ALL across the state.
For Alabama,
Kyle Sweetser

https://secure.actblue.com/donate/blu-sefc-q1-2026-em?refcode=2026-02-06 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/blu-sefc-q1-2026-em?refcode=2026-02-06]
You may have seen in the news [https://marylandmatters.org/2026/01/23/house-wastes-no-time-taking-up-congressional-redistricting-bill/] that the Governor’s Redistricting Advisory Commission sent a new map for Maryland’s congressional districts to the Maryland General Assembly. This discussion is Maryland’s response to the President’s and Republicans’ egregious mid-cycle redistricting spanning from Texas and Florida to Ohio, Missouri, North Carolina, and Utah.
I wanted you to hear this directly from me: while I don’t have a vote on the maps, I am ready to run in, win in, and serve in any district the General Assembly draws. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/blu-sefc-q1-2026-em?refcode=2026-02-06]
CONTRIBUTE TODAY [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/blu-sefc-q1-2026-em?refcode=2026-02-06]
The proposed map that has already passed the House of Delegates moves Annapolis – where I have represented in the State Senate and Congress for over seven years and where just bought my first home – and much of Anne Arundel County and Howard County from the Third District to the First District, which encompasses the Eastern Shore. I have never once considered running in a district that I don’t reside in. For the last seven years and over three tough elections, my neighbors have placed their trust in me to represent them. This November, I plan to ask them to place their trust in me once more, even if that means taking on the Chair of the Freedom Caucus.
Let’s be clear: I don’t have a say in these maps. I believe voters should decide who represents them – not the other way around. But if this map moves forward from the General Assembly to the Governor’s desk, I will hit the ground running – and I’ll need your help. Are you ready to pitch in? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/blu-sefc-q1-2026-em?refcode=2026-02-06]

# **Four Venezuelan migrants charged in $1 million SNAP fraud scheme across multiple states**
Four Venezuelan migrants in Massachusetts **[have been charged with defrauding the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) of up to $1 million](https://substack.com/redirect/5fcf5c6b-483e-4fcb-b754-604b404fc316?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** across six states and Puerto Rico by using stolen identities to obtain fraudulent benefits cards, which they used to stock El Primo Restaurant with free supplies and then sold menu items at complete profit.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5fcf5c6b-483e-4fcb-b754-604b404fc316?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Why it matters:** U.S. Attorney Leah Foley said the fraud included $440,000 connected to the restaurant scheme and up to $700,000 from fraudulent applications filed in the names of 100 stolen identities, with proceeds later wired to individuals in Venezuela and the Dominican Republic. Foley warned "it is no secret there is rampant fraud across this nation" and said to "anticipate seeing more and more of these cases coming here in Massachusetts."
* **The big picture:** The Massachusetts case is part of a nationwide pattern of benefits fraud. Maine recently paid out $45.6 million in improper payments for autism services with "unallowable services and questionable billing patterns," while Minnesota's massive Somali fraud involving hundreds of millions stolen from taxpayers is "probably overseas" and "impossible to get back," according to HHS Deputy Secretary Jim O'Neill. Foley criticized states with loose application processes, saying "any state that allows online applications without any ability to verify documents is leaving itself open to abuse."

* **What they 're doing:** The website provides tactics including contacting hotels, booking and canceling reservations to inconvenience ICE, and organizing "noise protests" with pots, pans, and whistles to ensure "ICE doesn't sleep." The site includes a map of "hotel ICE sightings" and reminds users to protect personally identifiable information using "best security practices" when harassing hotels.
* **The bigger picture:** The group also linked to a "Shut Out ICE" toolkit calling for preparations for a "general strike," describing it as "one of the most powerful tools that we can use to put pressure on the system." The toolkit instructs users to start community fundraisers for "strike funds" to support protesters' expenses including housing, utilities, and food. Anti-ICE protesters have recently used noise protests in Minneapolis, and according to a Daily Caller News Foundation report, activists are becoming increasingly accepting of militant behavior, with an "anarchist manifesto" calling "complete annihilation" of political opponents "essential."

# **Suspect who posed as Secret Service agent, threatened Trump killed in Portland shootout**
A suspect who falsely claimed to be a US Secret Service agent and threatened President Donald Trump **[was killed Saturday morning after allegedly opening fire on Portland Police officers](https://substack.com/redirect/ae302e5a-c65b-4ee7-8c4c-9ee4ccedab28?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** during a warrant execution at his apartment in Northwest Portland.
* **What happened:** The suspect entered a grocery store on January 31, pointed a handgun at a security guard while falsely claiming to be Secret Service, and pulled the trigger--but the gun did not fire. He fled the scene but left behind a case with a loaded shotgun containing "threatening messages written on the shotgun shells that specifically named President Donald Trump," prompting police to contact the actual Secret Service for assistance.
* **The confrontation:** Officers obtained an arrest warrant for first-degree attempted assault and arrived at the suspect's apartment at 5:15 am Thursday. After 35 minutes of failed negotiations and deploying tear gas, the suspect emerged from his unit allegedly armed with a handgun and "pointed a gun" at officers, according to police. Two Portland Police SERT officers fired shots, killing the suspect. Officers attempted to render medical aid, but paramedics determined he was deceased at the scene.
* **What 's next:** The two officers who used deadly force have been placed on administrative leave, and the investigation remains ongoing. The suspect's identity has not been released, and police have not provided additional details about the threatening messages written on shell casings mentioning Trump.

Dear Friend, This week made something very clear: when unelected institutions or political insiders try to override voters, State Freedom Caucus members are increasingly willing to draw firm lines — publicly and without apology.From Missouri to Wyoming and beyond, lawmakers are refusing to let major decisions get swept under the rug.Here’s what mattered this week.

**MISSOURI** The **Missouri Freedom Caucus** led a quiet but unmistakable show of force.For years, out-of-state activist groups have used the ballot initiative process to bypass Missouri lawmakers, ramming through policies that would never survive the legislative process. When the legislature tried to curb misleading ballot language, the Missouri Supreme Court struck the effort down.This week, the Court’s Chief Justice was scheduled to deliver the annual “State of the Judiciary” address before the legislature. **Missouri Freedom Caucus** members objected and House leadership agreed. The speech was canceled.This wasn’t about decorum. It was a signal. When unelected institutions act politically, legislators are not required to smile politely and pretend otherwise.**BOTTOM LINE:** Separation of powers doesn’t mean courts operate without accountability or criticism. The MOFC called them out.

* * *
_**by Ellie Leonard, BAM Contributing Editor**_
I've been digging through the Epstein files since July, 2025. That's it. I've done this for only six months, but in that time I've put in countless hours of bleary-eyed late nights, scrolling mind-numbing documents from photocopies of unpublished books, fully-redacted court cases, and endless email threads scheduling proffers, depositions, and airline tickets.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/19e4385b-cdc0-48c2-bc6a-76587b510a3a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Every so often we'll get a drop that interests the rest of the world, usually photos and videos. But after thousands of pictures of Epstein's water heaters, bookshelves, gravel pits, and empty memory cards, people get bored and shuffle out. The social media commentary dies down.
Not me.
I'm looking in those drawers filled with cosplay, wondering how it lines up with the dentist chair, and that weird Coney Island art on the walls. I wonder why a guy took a $60 million mansion and decorated it like a Hot Topic. I want to know what's on those blurry documents sitting on his desk. I'm reading every label of every floppy disk. I'm image-searching obscure sex toys (unbeknownst to me). I'm double-checking every redacted photo to see if I can find another copy online, careful to avoid AI fakes.
* * *
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYmx1ZWFtcC5jby9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.6KFsDNWU6809MiROJqFjVMaaDo6YXnPpGprR-1SHSn8?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=186891474)
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/19e4385b-cdc0-48c2-bc6a-76587b510a3a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
My favorites are the emails, those long threads of weird conversations that no one ever thought would be made public. Moments where bad men let their guard down and brag about their indiscretions, acting like little boys wondering "will she call me back?" when a 20-something flight attendant stops by their hotel room thousands of miles away. Academics suddenly like frat boys. Wall Street's finest toeing the line of their own sexual preference, just for favor from a guy who seemingly has it all and nothing at the same time. The descriptions of not just any girl, but a special one--young, blonde, skinny, childlike. Maybe she's 18, but she doesn't look like it.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/19e4385b-cdc0-48c2-bc6a-76587b510a3a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
I sometimes feel like the DOJ knows when I'm offline. It's impossible, but it always seems to line up with a kid's birthday or a trip into the city, and my phone blows up. This time I was headed in to hang out with [Aidan Wharton](https://substack.com/@aidanwharton), whom I'd met at the Substack Notes meetup last fall. "I like your nametag" I said, like an idiot. But the "[Gay Buffet](https://substack.com/redirect/497f2283-06f9-45ea-82a3-4a947a2f00c8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)" had a nice ring to it. Now he hosts the [Getting Close](https://substack.com/redirect/7192c921-b033-4f1a-b530-eaf8a46705b0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) podcast, and we'd set a time aside to really talk, face-to-face, with little glasses of tepid water and a professional setup. _Actual_ microphones, unlike my $30 sometimes-mic that lives half its life on my gamer kid's desk.
We had a lineup of questions that felt easy, kind of happy and banter-y. A just-right conversation between two new-old friends. But then Georgia Fort and Don Lemon were dragged from their sleep by masked FBI agents before daylight. Journalism was targeted yet again. And then they dropped the files, all 3.5 million of them. Coincidence? If you believe in that sort of thing...
* * *
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=3722532&post_id=186891474&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTg2ODkxNDc0LCJpYXQiOjE3NzAzOTQ1NTcsImV4cCI6MTc3Mjk4NjU1NywiaXNzIjoicHViLTM3MjI1MzIiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.ZpNfmWdgI7_k42Q-g5Lux0yr4-2AmtDAriUX390AIWM)
[](https://substack.com/redirect/e99fa118-9da1-46eb-bf34-837ef7675ddb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
While we chatted, I thought I could hear my phone buzzing, and buzzing, and buzzing through the closet wall where I'd hung my coat. I couldn't, but my brain wouldn't let go of those files. I knew what was waiting for me. I knew people wanted to know what I'd found. I knew influencers had already grabbed the biggest headlines and were posting wild and unexpected finds all over social media. Me, I was not in a hurry. Four-thousand files had been work. Thirty-thousand files had been a lot of work. 3.5 million files felt like a joke. So we chatted. I grabbed coffee. And I tried not to get carsick in the Uber home.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/91b2b284-9fb1-43b0-8ac1-b46b5106a786?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=3722532&post_id=186891474&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTg2ODkxNDc0LCJpYXQiOjE3NzAzOTQ1NTcsImV4cCI6MTc3Mjk4NjU1NywiaXNzIjoicHViLTM3MjI1MzIiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.ZpNfmWdgI7_k42Q-g5Lux0yr4-2AmtDAriUX390AIWM)
* * *
That night I began the first step, the same one I always do, in filtering through the files. I knew the DOJ wouldn't make it easy, and I was right--3.5 million _individual_ files, needing to be opened one at a time. Take too long, and you'll get timed out. Click the wrong thing, and you start all over again. _Purposefully difficult._ But like always, the world is filled with beautiful little tech geniuses, many of whom live on Substack, and we all found our massive piles of downloadable files to begin picking through. It meant upgrading our file-share systems; we could write it off on our taxes later. Upgrading Adobe, too; worth it. And then we waited for that slow download to tick by, thousands and thousands of pages at a time. Because remember, 3.5 million _files_ is not 3.5 million _pages._ A file could be anything--10, 20, 1000 pages. We were facing the Mount Everest of citizen journalism.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/32fd6dbc-9b26-42f1-9de7-b6585fe2cad5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
I downloaded Data Set 11 first, which felt doable. Gigantic of course, but nothing like the others. I shrunk it down into pdfs and sent it out to the internet sleuths to start to do their thing. Then I found batch 10, exponentially bigger than 11. It took me hours to download and I was just about to start compiling files when someone reached out with an SOS.
"DON'T OPEN DATA SET 10. WARNING: CSAM!"
I had no idea what CSAM was. I asked. _Child Sexual Abuse Material._
Apparently this was (or wasn't) a version of Data Set 10 that had not been redacted whatsoever, including imagery and video of children being abused. I deleted it immediately.
Then it became a terrible Easter egg hunt, where none of us knew if we had the wrong version of the files, the fully-unredacted documents of the Epstein case. No one wanted to accidentally happen upon something so heinous, but it was 3.5 million files. In the words of Ralphie Parker's old man: _There could be anything in there_.
[Ellie's Coffee Fund](https://substack.com/redirect/508e84d1-9850-4213-91a5-4a7157bbde14?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
I sat back and did some thinking on Friday night, while I compiled what I had. Don Lemon and Georgia Fort, along with a host of other independent journalists had just been arrested for reporting the news. Not participating. Not inciting. Just showing up and hitting record. TikTok, which was purchased by ByteDance in January, had begun recording all of our data, whether we posted something or not, blocking videos from independent journalists and banning their accounts. Twitter continues to shadow-ban links to independent media articles and videos, especially Substack. And stories that I'd participated in were now on Donald Trump's radar. Literally the President of the United States.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/19e4385b-cdc0-48c2-bc6a-76587b510a3a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
And it struck me that it was no accident that we'd received an unredacted version of these files. Because the DOJ had promised us for months that they were dragging their feet so as to keep survivors safe, and redact their names and information out of the files and away from prying eyes. Yet [Aaron Parnas](https://substack.com/@aaronparnas) found documents with children's faces and information, including drivers' licenses and birth records. (_He 's since contacted the DOJ, who removed the file.)_ And there are still pages of CSAM hidden in the files on average citizens' hard drives, unbeknownst to them, as they dig and do their due diligence to society in the name of helping survivors.
* * *

They only came from one place. And they only came for one reason.

We have created a beautiful, and very big, community of citizen journalists to protect the rights of kids and create a better world moving forward that includes justice and accountability. Subscribe to support Ellie's new show! by Ellie Leonard, BAM Contributing Editor I've been digging through the Epstein files since July, 2025. That's it.
