# [One word: WOW](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=6380051&post_id=187096009&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTg3MDk2MDA5LCJpYXQiOjE3NzA0MDQ1NzEsImV4cCI6MTc3Mjk5NjU3MSwiaXNzIjoicHViLTYzODAwNTEiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.eHE620SAWw7lwo8SrMTBw0SKzZYOZo4AgETh3_q5LAI)
### What this grassroots team tells me about Michigan, this incredible moment, and our fight ahead
| | [Haley Stevens](https://substack.com/@haleyformi)
---
| Feb 6
---
| [](https://substack.com/@haleyformi)
---

---
| | | [](https://substack..mLdv2WFmdd5N6G6U8kXRFoOejNNJdHn5cjwo8Efy0uk?&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email)
---
| | [READ IN APP](https://open.substack.com/pub/haleyformi/p/one-word-wow?utm_source=email&redirect=app-store&utm_campaign=email-read-in-app)
---

My friends.**One word:**_**WOW.**_
This team just did something incredible.
When the FEC numbers came in for the final quarter of 2025, and I saw that **this grassroots team outraised Mike Rogers** , I had to stop for a minute. I had to sit with it.
Because it meant something real.
People showed up.
Regular working people: teachers, nurses, retirees, clergy members, small business owners. Folks who squeezed a few extra dollars out of their budgets because they believe Michigan, and our country, deserve something better.
So I want to say this clearly: _Thank you._
I'm genuinely blown away.
I've spent a lot of time lately talking with Michiganders across the state, and everywhere I go, I hear the same mix of emotions.
People are so proud of this state - they love where they're from. But they're worried about what comes next, and they're fed up with the chaos coming out of Washington. _I get it._
And when I shake someone's hand or give someone a hug, I sense something else, too -- a quiet strength and a steady determination to keep fighting for something better.
That's this grassroots team. That's this moment.
Outraising Mike Rogers isn't just a number on a spreadsheet. It's a signal. It tells me people are paying attention -- they're engaged. They believe this campaign is worth fighting for.
And it tells me something else, too: **We 're in it now.**
A new poll shows Mike Rogers and me statistically tied -- and they show I'm the Democrat with the best shot at defeating him.
That's not about ego. _It 's about responsibility._
Everyone knows Michigan is a battleground. One that could determine control of the U.S. Senate. And when a race is this close, momentum matters.
Because the truth is, when grassroots momentum shows up like this, it doesn't go unnoticed.
MAGA billionaires have already spent millions backing Mike Rogers. And after this fundraising report? I promise you, Donald Trump and his megadonors will be laser-focused on our race.
But that's OK.**This is Michigan.**
We don't back down just because a fight gets harder.
We show up. We stand together. We work harder.
That's how my parents ran their small landscaping business. That's how we helped save 200,000 Michigan jobs during the 2009 auto rescue. And that's the spirit behind this campaign.
So when I say "thank you," I don't just mean for the dollars. I mean for the belief. For the trust. For choosing to fight for a better future.
We've got a long road ahead. But moments like this remind me why I raised my hand to serve the state I love. And why I know, deep down, that we'll win.
**If you 're in a position to chip in and help us keep this momentum going, I'd be so grateful. As we've seen, every contribution, no matter the size, truly makes a difference.**
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/314637f5-454e-4678-a49d-fcaf479b909d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Let's keep going.
With grit and gratitude,
Haley
* * *

A personal note from Haley 👋

I'm a lifelong Michigander and the daughter of small-business owners. I've spent my career fighting for Michigan's working families - and now I'm running for the U.S. Senate to keep standing up for the people I love.

But here's the truth: Senate control could come down to Michigan. And Trump and his megadonors know it. That's why they're gearing up to spend tens of millions to defeat me and hand this seat to a MAGA Republican.

I need your help to fight back. This race will be one of the most competitive - and expensive - in the country, and I'm counting on grassroots support to win.

If you're with me, will you chip in today?

Email is one of the most important ways that we can keep you informed on this critical race, but if you want to stop receiving emails from us, [**click here**](https://act.angela4congress.com/unsubscribe/unsubscribe/?t=2&akid=311%2E66908%2E0Mzk9v).

Friend — as we recognize and celebrate Black History Month, I want to reflect on what it means here in California.
Black Californians have long been at the forefront of movements for justice, dignity, and collective care — often without recognition, yet _always_ with courage. Their leadership shaped our labor movement, our fight for civil rights, and our vision for what a more just future can look like.
Here is a list of my favorite reads by Black female authors who have informed my own personal politics and worldview:
* Angela Davis: Are Prisons Obsolete
* Tricia Hersey: Rest Is Resistance
* Yaa Gyasi: Homegoing
* Toni Morrison: Beloved
* Eve Ewing: Original Sins: The (Mis)education of Black and Native Children and the Construction of American Racism

But, honoring this history _can’t_ be limited to one month. It asks us to keep learning, listening, and showing up year-round to understand the lived experiences of Black individuals and support the work being done **[by people in](https://act.angela4congress.com/go/823?t=3&akid=311%2E66908%2E0Mzk9v) **Congress**[today by advocating for reparations to the descendents of enslaved people](https://act.angela4congress.com/go/823?t=4&akid=311%2E66908%2E0Mzk9v) **and prison abolition advocates.
In solidarity,
Angela for Congress

body:
These USPS postmark changes are just the latest step taken by MAGA's vote suppressors to limit mail-in ballots.
Why? Because in recent elections, the percentage of people voting by mail hasn't favored their extremist candidates, and voter participation has actually increased via the use of vote-by-mail and drop boxes. This all leads to candidates MAGA doesn't like winning elections.
Team, these changes are about who has power now and how badly they want to keep it. RUSH $35 or more right now help inform voters of this change and defend the use of mail-in ballots across the country >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=020626_2&amount=35]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
HuffPost: Mail-In Voters Could Face A New Obstacle This Midterm Season [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=020626_2&amount=25]
Team: Changes at the U.S. Postal Service are going to make a known problem even worse, and it could affect thousands of voters across the country in this November’s midterm elections.
Legally speaking, the date stamped on your mail is when it counts as being sent, from your bills to your taxes to your ballot. For decades, that's been stamped the day you gave it to the United States Postal Service (USPS), whether you handed it to your mail carrier, left it in a mailbox, or dropped it at the local post office.
That's no longer the case. Your mail will be stamped the day it hits a regional processing facility , not your local post office. That could be a day, or more, later than when you handed your mail over, thanks to the Trump administration's "cost-cutting" efforts.
How does this impact vote-by-mail? If you live in a state with a mail-in ballot grace period -- something most states still have, even though MAGA is trying to end those -- your ballot still counts if it was postmarked by Election Day and received in the grace period after Election Day. In this case, however, a ballot mailed on Election Day may not be postmarked as Election Day, making your ballot automatically invalid even though you followed the rule of law and the postmark date is out of your control.
We have to make sure every voter understands this change and how it can impact them -- from vote-by-mail, to their bills, their taxes, legal replies to companies, everything. What Americans think is the mailing deadline may not be the deadline anymore and that's a huge deal that's being under-reported by the media.
Team, Every voter needs to know about this massive change. Will you pitch in $35 or whatever you can today and help us spread the word about the USPS changes so we can protect mail-in ballots? >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=020626_2&amount=35]
If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:

We're worried about every mail-in voter getting their ballot in on time, but especially those most vulnerable to this change, like the elderly, rural Americans who live far from USPS regional facilities, our military service members, and young people who are voting by mail away from home. None of them deserve to be disenfranchised from our elections over DOGE's cost-cutting measures.
Whether you can fuel our work today or not, we appreciate your support and we hope you can spread the word about this USPS change to your friends, family, and colleagues. You never know how a quick mention of something like this news might truly impact someone else's life.
Thank you,

Legally speaking, the date stamped on your mail is when it counts as being sent, from your bills to your taxes to your ballot. For decades, that's been stamped the day you gave it to the United States Postal Service (USPS), whether you handed it to your mail carrier, left it in a mailbox, or dropped it at the local post office. That's no longer the case. Your mail will be stamped the day it hits a regional processing facility , not your local post office. That could be a day, or more, later than when you handed your mail over, thanks to the Trump administration's "cost-cutting" efforts. How does this impact vote-by-mail? If you live in a state with a mail-in ballot grace period -- something most states still have, even though MAGA is trying to end those -- your ballot still counts if it was postmarked by Election Day and received in the grace period after Election Day. In this case, however, a ballot mailed on Election Day may not be postmarked as Election Day, making your ballot automatically invalid even though you followed the rule of law and the postmark date is out of your control. We have to make sure every voter understands this change and how it can impact them -- from vote-by-mail, to their bills, their taxes, legal replies to companies, everything. _Forwarded Message:_

Peter,

Last week, Marie asked you to weigh in on how increased healthcare costs are impacting you, your family, or your business. The responses were overwhelming: **More than 80% of respondents reported rising costs that are putting a real strain on budgets.**

People told us the same story again and again: premiums that rise every year, copays that keep climbing, prescription drugs that cost more month after month. For too many families, and especially seniors on Medicare, healthcare has become a constant source of stress instead of a basic promise.

No one should have to choose between groceries and medicine, or delay care because they’re worried about the next bill.

That’s why Marie is fighting to protect Medicare, lower out-of-pocket costs, and take on the corporate interests driving healthcare prices higher – not cut benefits or shift more costs onto families who are already stretched thin.

In response, President Trump tweeted more than a dozen times, calling for me to be investigated, arrested, and hanged.

Since then, the FBI and former Fox News host Jeanine Pirro, now U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia, asked to interview me for the inquiry.

Peter Willis,

Right now, communities across Minneapolis and the rest of the country are
fighting for their lives – while deportation oligarchs and corporations
rake in billions helping ICE terrorize our neighborhoods.

One of those companies is Enterprise Car Rental, which provides about $80
MILLION in rental car services to the federal government, including
countless vehicles to ICE.

It's unconscionable. Which is why Our Revolution is deploying our
grassroots network to call out Enterprise to stop enabling ICE’s horror
NOW – and we need you to join us.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/35061?source=email-20260206&t=1011&akid=10186%2E5885482%2Ea-ljTr ]Take action: Add your name to pressure Enterprise to stop fueling ICE’s
inhumane takeover of our cities NOW!

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/35061?source=email-20260206&t=1013&akid=10186%2E5885482%2Ea-ljTr ]Enterprise protest photo

Make no mistake: by providing ICE with the cars they use to kidnap members
of our communities, Enterprise is helping this regime to terrorize our
families and rip people from their homes and schools.

We cannot allow corporations to continue getting away with getting richer
off our fear and suffering. Yet that’s exactly what Enterprise is doing.

We know public pressure works. When our movement organized against Avelo
Airlines for collaborating with Trump’s regime and forced the airline to
stop operating out of several airports, we showed what’s possible.

Now, it's time to come after Enterprise – and our teams are already doing
the work, organizing actions in St. Louis and beyond. In Minnesota – our
on the ground organizers are also working with local electeds to push for
an eviction moratorium and support for at-home learning. And in Maryland,
we’re organizing to pass a bill to stop ICE agents from hiding behind face
masks.

Grassroots organizing is how we stop ICE. Now, we need a tidal wave of
support from across the country to up the pressure on Enterprise
executives to act.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/35061?source=email-20260206&t=1014&akid=10186%2E5885482%2Ea-ljTr ]Add your name right now and send a powerful message: Enterprise, drop

Together, let’s force Enterprise to pick a side.

When we organize, we win,

name: Wes Moore
subject: How can we make this Maryland’s decade?
body:
While we’re in the legislative session, I want to hear from you.
# [](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/8?t=1&akid=1220%2E1086043%2E4Xeekw)
While it seems like so much dysfunction has taken over down in Washington, we have a chance to enact a bold agenda at the state level.
Peter, right now in Annapolis my team, the legislature, and I are hard at work making this Maryland’s decade. But we’re missing one critical voice in that work: You.
So I wanted to reach out to you directly and hear more about what is on your mind: **What issues are most important to you right now? What should my team and I tackle next?**
Whether it’s bringing down costs, creating new jobs, funding our public schools, or standing up for Marylanders, I want to make sure I hear from this dedicated grassroots team.
**[Please, take our survey today to let us know what you want us to prioritize in 2026 and beyond.](https://act.wesmoore.com/signup/moore-2026-issues-survey/?source=em20260206&t=2&akid=1220%2E1086043%2E4Xeekw)**
**[Share your thoughts](https://act.wesmoore.com/signup/moore-2026-issues-survey/?source=em20260206&t=3&akid=1220%2E1086043%2E4Xeekw)**
Elevate,
Wes

| | | Trump lost in Georgia in 2020.

But his sore loser's crusade continues.

This week, the President called on Republicans to nationalize and "TAKE OVER" elections (!)

This immediately after the FBI — alongside Tulsi Gabbard, the nation's spy chief — RAIDED a Georgia election office and seized truckloads of 2020 ballots.

From Minnesota to Georgia, we are watching the President unravel as he abuses federal power to pursue vendettas and consolidate power.

My reelection in Georgia is among the most critical U.S. Senate contests in 2026.

And with Trump working to "TAKE OVER" elections — including in Georgia — we will win this race ONLY if we defend Georgians' voting rights from his schemes.

Remember: Georgia has always been ground zero for his conspiracy theories. Remember when he demanded our state's election officials "find" him the votes to win in a state he had lost?

**_So: how do we ensure fair midterm elections?_**

We have to triple down on voter mobilization and voter protection.

We have to win by decisive margins and we have to protect voting rights.

That means investing the resources needed to turn out every Democrat in the midterms, and to make sure every vote is properly cast, protected, and counted.

Look: Georgia voters don't take kindly when folks try to intimidate them or prevent them from voting. All of this will only MOTIVATE them to vote in record numbers.

name: MassDems featuring Kip Diggs
subject: A Reflection on Service from Rep. Kip Diggs
disclaimer_text: Paid for by the Massachusetts Democratic State Committee
body:
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP31/1/93809/images/Logo.png]
Dear Friends,
Black History Month invites us to reflect on service and how it shapes lives across generations. In my family, that history picks up with Robert and Mitchell Higginbotham, both Tuskegee Airmen. They served a country that denied them full recognition, yet they carried out their duty with precision and resolve. Their example was not about recognition. It was about responsibility and commitment to doing the work that needed to be done.
That standard carried forward with my father, George Diggs, who served two tours in the Army during the Vietnam War. His experience left a lasting mark on how he viewed duty, family, and perseverance. Outside of the military, my family operated a small local business on Cape Cod where trust mattered and your word meant something. Service was not talked about as an idea. It showed up in how you treated people every day and how you took your obligations to heart.
As a young man, boxing became my way into the big, wide world. It gave me structure and discipline at a formative time in my life. Through the sport, I traveled, met people from different places, and learned what it meant to earn respect through effort. Boxing teaches you quickly that you do not succeed alone. Coaches guide you. Training partners push you. Even opponents play a role in your growth. Those lessons stayed with me and helped me to achieve success.
Later in life, service took on a more personal weight. I lost my son and my brother to drunk drivers. That kind of loss forces you to decide how you will move forward. I chose to stay engaged and to channel that grief into work that could make communities safer and more connected. I was able to do that because my community stepped in and stood with me when it mattered most.
Service does not belong to one role or one moment. It can look like military duty, public office, or community leadership. It can also look like caring for a neighbor, running an honest business, or showing up when someone is struggling. At its core, service is about accountability to one another and a belief that shared effort, being part of a team, leads to better outcomes.
Black history is filled with people who understood this truth. They leaned on collective strength and stayed rooted in their communities. Their progress came from persistence and cooperation, not shortcuts. Those lessons remain relevant in Massachusetts in how we govern and how we live together.
Service is not about a title or a moment. It is the daily work of showing up with integrity, listening, and doing right by the people you serve – God bless.
Kip Diggs [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP31/1/93809/images/Rep.%20Kip%20Diggs.png]
State Representative, 2nd Barnstable District

| [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124872649/599973674/-3547583?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjAxMjk1ODdiLTk2MDMtZjExMS04MzJmLTAwMGQzYTFmMGU0YyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=gqzuccKOr9M_u7OWY2z86Uq2xKalj5Wx81XvUgfMZrw=&emci=40acb236-7d03-f111-832f-000d3a1f0e4c&emdi=0129587b-9603-f111-832f-000d3a1f0e4c&ceid=8431045)

Peter, can you believe that the midterms are nine months away and we still have no clue what the final congressional map will look like? At this very moment, several states are still planning to redraw their maps and the Supreme Court is set to rule on an essential protection in the Voting Rights Act, which could send other states into a last minute redistricting scramble. That’s not how it’s supposed to work, but Republicans care more about clinging to power than democratic norms. Their House majority is now just a handful of seats. Rather than face the will of the people this November, the Trump administration is in overdrive to rig the maps in their favor. President Trump is terrified of what losing control of Congress would mean — he even said aloud that he’s worried about being impeached (again). So he’s plunged our nation into a redistricting crisis instead. **Our fight against ongoing Republican efforts to manipulate maps and silence voters is as essential as ever.[Your support for NDRC will go a long way to ensure that the will of the people prevails in November — and yes, which party ultimately controls Congress for the rest of Trump's presidency. ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124872653/599973679/-2069046819?refcode=don_ndrc_tier1_email_MidtermPreview_email_20260206-NDRC-Tier1-MidtermPreview_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20260206-NDRC-Tier1-MidtermPreview_&utm_campaign=MidtermPreview&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjAxMjk1ODdiLTk2MDMtZjExMS04MzJmLTAwMGQzYTFmMGU0YyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=gqzuccKOr9M_u7OWY2z86Uq2xKalj5Wx81XvUgfMZrw=)** President Trump is mounting even more pressure on Republican lawmakers to give in to his redistricting crisis. He and his anti-democracy allies have shown they’ll stop at nothing to hold on to power. It says a lot that they know that a fair election won’t go their way. The NDRC is on the case 24/7 to defend free and fair elections in every state where Republicans are attempting to gain an unfair advantage. We’re ready to leap into action whenever the Supreme Court ruling comes down. **But the threats to democracy are mounting and we need more resources than ever to sustain our critical response. ** [**Help fund our work in the weeks ahead so we can protect our democracy and stop Trump from getting away with this redistricting scam.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124872663/599973687/-2069046819?refcode=don_ndrc_tier1_email_MidtermPreview_email_20260206-NDRC-Tier1-MidtermPreview_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20260206-NDRC-Tier1-MidtermPreview_&utm_campaign=MidtermPreview&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjAxMjk1ODdiLTk2MDMtZjExMS04MzJmLTAwMGQzYTFmMGU0YyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=gqzuccKOr9M_u7OWY2z86Uq2xKalj5Wx81XvUgfMZrw=)

Peter,
Happy Black History Month.
This month isn’t just about looking back. It’s about honoring our history by fighting in the present. Our ancestors built this country with courage, resistance, and a relentless demand for justice. They didn’t wait for permission, and neither should we.
Right now, we’re seeing history repeat itself. Communities are under attack. Rights are being stripped away. People are being silenced. And every day, the work of protecting Black voices and Black futures falls on us.
So this month, we can’t just celebrate. We must stand, act, and lift up Black lives, remembering that the same power that drove generations of Black people to make change still lives within us today.
Our history isn’t just behind us, it’s alive in the work we do, the streets we march, and the policies we fight for. And it’s our responsibility to make sure the next generation inherits a world that sees and values them fully.
This Black History Month, let’s honor our past by fighting for our future, together .
In solidarity,
Cori Bush

It’s a voter suppression bill House Republicans are putting on the floor this week. 33 GOP members of the Senate are co-sponsoring it. And if it goes on to pass, it’s going to make it much harder for Servicemembers AND Veterans to vote.

name: Roy Cooper
subject: Asking for your trust, and your first $5 donation
body:
This race is just too important to sit by.
|
# [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/2365?source=&t=1&akid=502%2E124072%2EE8Mg9l)
Peter, the first time I ever ran for public office, it was right in the place where I was born and raised — Nash County, NC. Getting the chance to serve the people of my home community in North Carolina’s legislature meant so much. It meant even more that people put their trust in me. The fact is, I’ve never wanted to leave North Carolina at all. This state is my home, and it’s where I planned to serve. But our nation is at a tipping point, and this race matters so much to so many of us. I couldn’t just sit by. So I’m asking for your help this evening because too much is on the line — and because our team is facing our biggest financial challenge yet, just five days from now. We’re required by the FEC to file a public financial report ahead of North Carolina’s primary. It’s our best chance to show our GOP opponent that the people are with us as we begin the general election campaign. We set a goal of earning 10,000 grassroots contributions by our deadline on Wednesday, and I would like to see your name on our list. **[Peter, are you with me? Falling behind would really set us back — and give our far-right opponent and outside attack groups the opportunity to seize the momentum. I’m personally asking you to put your trust in me today. Pitch in just $5 or any amount that fits in your budget to help meet our goal.](https://act.roycooper.com/go/1898?refcode=em_RC_FR_Filing6_020626&amount=5&t=7&akid=502%2E124072%2EE8Mg9l)** | [DONATE](https://act.roycooper.com/go/5359?t=8&akid=502%2E124072%2EE8Mg9l)
---
Thanks so much,
Roy
[](https://act.roycooper.com/go/5359?t=9&akid=502%2E124072%2EE8Mg9l)
* * *
Democrat Roy Cooper is running for U.S. Senate to help take back the Majority for Democrats. North Carolina is Democrats’ best chance to flip a seat from red to blue — the path to stopping Republicans in Washington starts here.

National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us.

Cooper is a former state legislator, Attorney General, and most recently Governor of North Carolina. North Carolina will be the most competitive Senate election of 2026, and Cooper enters the race as the most formidable candidate of either party.

Cooper’s signature achievements include helping to expand Medicaid and helping make NC the top state for business by creating thousands of jobs and growing the clean energy economy.

| | Fellow Patriot,
---
| | Charlie Kirk lived fast. And he lived loud.

He filled arenas. He lit a fire in the next generation on campus.

He confronted lies and spoke truth with boldness.

And he built a movement and a machine that few ever thought possible.

I saw it up close -- _Charlie moved at a pace most couldn 't keep up with. _

But in the middle of all the noise... he made a quiet decision that changed everything.

_**He started observing the Sabbath. **_

Not as a box to check. Not as a religious performance.

_But as an act of obedience. _

As a way of saying, **_" God, You are enough. And because You are enough, I need not carry the weight of a world that was never mine to hold." _**

Every week -- no matter what -- Charlie stopped.

He turned off the noise. He stepped away from the battlefield.

No email. No media. No work.

He gave his full attention fully to God, his wife Erika, and his children.

It was hard at first -- for someone who carried so much.

But over time, it changed him.

And before he was assassinated, he wrote a book about what he had learned...

clean_body: It wasn’t about politics...| | | | | Fellow Patriot, | | Charlie Kirk lived fast. And he lived loud. He filled arenas. He lit a fire in the next generation on campus. He confronted lies and spoke truth with boldness. And he built a movement and a machine that few ever thought possible. I saw it up close -- Charlie moved at a pace most couldn 't keep up with. But in the middle of all the noise... he made a quiet decision that changed everything. He started observing the Sabbath. Not as a box to check. Not as a religious performance. But as an act of obedience. As a way of saying, " God, You are enough. And because You are enough, I need not carry the weight of a world that was never mine to hold." Every week -- no matter what -- Charlie stopped. He turned off the noise. He stepped away from the battlefield. No email. No media. No work. He gave his full attention fully to God, his wife Erika, and his children. It was hard at first -- for someone who carried so much. But over time, it changed him. And before he was assassinated, he wrote a book about what he had learned... This was Charlie's final message. His final act of trust. A book not about politics... but about peace. It 's called: Stop, in the Name of God. - Fellow Patriot, like I mentioned, this isn't a political book. It's not a culture war manifesto. It's a call to stop. To rest. To breathe. To return to God. Because Charlie believed America hadn 't just forgotten truth... It had forgotten trust. Trust that the world keeps spinning when you step away. Trust that God is in control. Trust that rest is not weakness -- it's worship. In Stop, in the Name of God, you'll discover: 🔥 How Charlie reclaimed the Sabbath in a world built on burnout 🔥 What sacred rest gave back to him -- as a father, husband, and believer 🔥 Why he believed this message could spark revival in a restless generation Charlie wrote this book because he knew what it meant to nearly lose his peace -- and what it felt like to find it again. That's the heartbeat of his final message. - Charlie Kirk didn't waste his time on earth. He left behind a family. He left behind a movement. And he left behind this truth... For anyone ready to step off the treadmill... and walk back toward what's eternal. Fellow Patriot, thank you -- in advance -- for helping reach the next generation with truth, faith, and moral courage. These are the very things Charlie gave his life for. May the message he left behind lead you -- just as it led him -- to a deeper trust in God... A stronger love for your family... And a renewed peace in your own soul. ## Kentucky Family Brings Calf Indoors
A Kentucky family [brought a newborn calf](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOrCAYhZ9GOwyCwlhQ3MZubrsl-YWfkR0EA8y4vv3GTfYJtjvJSb6c73zc9R188PHxHzZU7uF0dUlHPErAWjHrJ8b6Ms_TQHA7xh1CgWghRc0oE4QyQoW24MOph9Yqh8iQt6h6KenQ93Ic21VxOQqHBsTgRueWyYKYpOUT9Lcbx-nWenXRKKOC9ZRx1jkpBgNcLtxyuYBpBorW15S7z-RjXdGFM70xdyZtbVBrrXtp-L-GzQ2bj-PozFIui6tv2HzFhs2_MsTB5sNJyoqhYi4k4rGkHMllSfCrZtyQmBQsqbjtmKG-Ml6ENiu7Hz4EX4RsBvrYwIefEfXP770V-w4AAP__cIGJEw) inside their Mount Sterling home during a weekend deep freeze, where it cuddled on the couch with their two young children after struggling in single-digit temperatures. Macey Sorrell said the calf was "just frozen" when her husband found it Saturday morning, with its umbilical cord resembling a popsicle. After losing a calf to frostbite last winter, the family moved quickly to warm the newborn with a blow dryer and clean off the ice and afterbirth. The couple's 3-year-old son Gregory named the calf Sally after his favorite movie character and snuggled beside her on the couch. The heartwarming [photos show the children](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOnjAQhJ8Guv1ljMFc4SIN3aVNiYy9hs1vvMiYQ-TpI5JHuG40I43mm1-f06elSGn5aTc0YQlTCTwlvI6IpWCe3pjK6d63szHsmHYbD5u85TRJIXsQEkQ_eUvxnlTtTUCU2NZoGq2FahrddfVqPlTjrHSu77zo8cN1rZbDoAaltRs61dRknjYhRS8bIVv5CrpXzrZ6bn2rZ-sqJdBT4fz6zZTKiiHe_IX55Xiro1lL2Y-q_VHJsZLjmzd-EJ6wkuMjKzlyCDPa8t-YOSd4mODC6HhDD5QO8gj-zJQW8Ig7hIz4B6EwuNP7iMAJHJ9uhZD5KDBTQbgoFcwQ7EbxBrdS9BlTnY3fL4qRjl5XSiybpfhvbfn2zV9G_g0AAP__OauXEQ) cuddling with the fluffy calf on their furniture. The family reunited Sally with her mother the next morning, and both are doing well on the farm where the Sorrells keep about three dozen cows.
## Teen Climbers Rescue Stranded Hikers
Two teenage boys [rescued five unprepared adults](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDuOgzAUAE8DnSN_AJPCxTbpsu2W6GE_EyfmGdkmiNuvslfYeqTRaH7u0x1CDLR8w4rGL36qPk2ER4lYK-bphVR3-zotRL8hbRALkINEk-RyYFwyPkwOQjynrnXGI0pULRqhNe-E0H3fPoziQ484a9nDlc9XKUYJvRVg_Sg4R9UG87FxyQcpuFTy4vXQWVB6Vk7pGWzTcXShpnx5pkD1gT6e6Y35YtPaRvOodSuN-mrkrZG3DdMW8YMaeauIBAuyOZ2FZSx2R1ZqBnLoGLg91sIOhBxoYU8EKqwQwgtzYT6nlRVKx8nWtFOFQCwHtyATYrx2vBvbbNx2hBhDGXTT8WWFEP-a6r9nvo38DQAA__-tsY0h) and a small dog stranded on England's third-highest mountain after finding them wearing jeans and sneakers with no climbing equipment on the snowy ridge. Rowan Kay, 15, and Caelan Blades, 16, were ice climbing down Helvellyn mountain on Jan. 10 when they spotted the struggling group frozen on Striding Edge. One woman was slipping around "like she was on a treadmill" without gloves or crampons while carrying her dog, with another having a panic attack from the conditions. The teens spent 30 minutes helping the group down in a zigzag pattern, guiding them step by step to safety. The Patterdale Mountain Rescue Team later praised the boys' "strong mountain skills" and maturity, calling them potential future mountain rescuers. See [the photos of the teens here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGO3CAYBOCnwd1Z8P8YQkGR08qpLm1KhOFnTRaDZZOz9u2jTaS8QOr5NBrNjw_34XPJ9f7db2TTPbmemqt0nYV6p8M9qPZf4fEMvqSd6u7L6Wv0rTrgoN44vHHlos_l6eQQbSICwoGs0JpLIfQ0DatdNHjBjQjThELylKQEAxI0foloBA3Zvto4cAWCA8KYtJLBo14wol58YJJTzL0d48-Wa18plWf7pGMMbRuKXXvfT4ZfGcwM5uu6xuQDLa09XoDBvK-tt1eKc1pyZHgTYIRBbYxCjnJSDJTfdobvJ3WGtz0s419iQBmFSin4R0oLvhDDG1X37X04bNyvXEo-lWaS3zefy59h_b8f_bTwOwAA__9idoVC).

body:
Deep State bureaucrats declared total war with no rules and no mercy

---
Friend,
I want to take you back in history for a moment, and you’ll very quickly understand why.

Forty-seven years ago, in the shadow of Soviet tanks and communist oppression, Pope John Paul II stepped onto Polish soil for the first time in thirty-one years and spoke three simple words:

_**“Be not afraid.”**_

Millions had gathered there in Warsaw’s Victory Square. The regime trembled. And within a decade, the Berlin Wall lay in rubble.

**Paired together with courageous political leadership from Ronald Reagan and Margaret Thatcher,_faith – spoken boldly – had triumphed over fear._**

Today, that same spirit is under siege – not in Poland, but in places like **Nigeria, Sudan and even South Korea.**

**Consider Leah Sharibu, a brave 15-year-old Christian schoolgirl in Nigeria.** In 2018, Islamic State barbarians abducted 110 girls from her school. While 104 were returned and five tragically killed, they kept Leah – as punishment for her **unyielding refusal to renounce Christ and convert to Islam.** Now, many years later, she remains in captivity with ISWAP (Islamic State West Africa Province), who threaten to hold her as a "slave for life."

And yet, this is just one example facing Christians in Nigeria. Since 2009, there have been a reported **19,000 churches destroyed** , **over 100,000 killed** and **at least 5 million more displaced.** The data reveal that for every one Muslim, 5.2 Christians are killed.

**In Sudan** , Islamist paramilitaries known as the Rapid Support Forces have been on a rampage, **bombing churches** , and **killing priests and worshippers sheltering inside while forcing survivors to convert or be killed** – in some cases, **_crucified_**. **Over 150,000 have died in the conflict, many hunted and targeted for their faith.** This ongoing conflict has resulted in a catastrophic humanitarian crisis, including mass displacement, severe food insecurity, and the complete collapse of public services.

**In South Korea** , a nation we rebuilt and have defended for 75 years, the new government with communist sympathies has been **arresting pastors, seizing church records, and even jailed an 82-year-old religious leader for leading prayer.**

And if you think this is only an international problem, I ask you to think back just a couple of years, when **pro-life grandmothers – _women in their 70s and 80s_ – were handcuffed and imprisoned by Joe Biden’s DOJ for peacefully praying outside abortion clinics.**

I don’t share these tragic, gruesome facts to paralyze you with despair, but to rally you to act. And here’s how...

**Save the Persecuted Christians** is an organization that has been effectively fighting on the front lines of this battle – **leading a 200+ group coalition to amplify survivors’ voices, awaken the public and policymakers, and drive direct action to hold the perpetrators accountable.**

In fact, they played a key role in the successful effort to encourage President Trump to designate Nigeria as a “Country of Particular Concern” (CPC), officially laying the groundwork for targeted sanctions and other measures.

| | | | | **2026 February e-newsletter**
####
---
|
* USF grad students look toward a future of public service
* M.P. Brown students get a lesson in civil liberties at 500 County Center
* It was a privilege to fight for public transit while serving on the MTC
* Sacred Heart Prep, Daly City team up to renovate Marchbank Park Field

---
| | |
---
|
# “Caltrain will connect all the Super Bowl activities this week from north to south and is the safest, greenest way to travel the Peninsula in comfort.”
# **\- Supervisor David Canepa**
---
| | | | **2026 February e-newsletter** **Battle brews over illegal fence blocking access to Thornton State Beach** Dear friends, I’m standing with our community to protect public access to Thornton State Beach in Daly City, a coastline that belongs to everyone because over the past three weeks, an 8-foot chain-link fence was erected on private land that blocks the only public access trail down to the beach. Even more alarming, a hand-drawn sign warning trespassers they would be shot was posted on the fence. This situation raises serious safety concerns and I’m urging the California Coastal Commission to step in, oppose these restrictions and require the removal of the fence to restore lawful public access to Thornton State Beach. The California Coastal Act clearly states private landowners cannot block public access to the sea. Our beaches are public resources and I will continue to fight to keep them open and accessible for all. There is only one trail down to the beach from Olympic Way in Daly City. This multi-use trail is a popular destination for recreation extending from the scenic bluffs and cliffs overlooking Thornton State Beach all the way down to the water. As a nearby resident, I routinely hike down to the beach from the parking area at the end of Thornton Beach Loop but the chain link fence currently restricts trail access to the beach. I’m confident the fence will be removed soon and access restored to the beach but until it is, I urge all visitors to the park to remain vigilant.
**Sacred Heart Prep, Daly City team up to renovate Marchbank Park Field** I was proud to join Sacred Heart Cathedral President Melinda Skrade, John Vigo and the entire SHC team recently at the groundbreaking for the historic renovation of Marchbank Park Field in Daly City. Together with Daly City Mayor Glenn Sylvester, Vice Mayor Teresa Proaño, Councilman Rod Daus-Magbual, Councilwoman Juslyn Manalo, City Manager Tom Piccolotti and the Daly City community they are providing a truly world-class facility for Daly City residents that will serve generations to come. Seeing this vision take shape is something our entire community can celebrate. This is a public-private partnership between Sacred Heart Cathedral Preparatory and Daly City to renovate the existing Marchbank Field which is underutilized. The project includes new replacement artificial turf, batting cages, improved bleachers for spectators, and facilities that will support multiple sports, as well as new sub-drainage system, field lighting, perimeter fencing and retaining walls. Seeing this vision take shape is something our entire community can celebrate. It reflects our shared commitment to youth opportunity, community pride, and healthy, active spaces where families and students can gather, play and build memories. I can’t wait to see the finished field and all the future generations who will benefit from this investment in our community, from athletes to families who simply want a place to play, connect and thrive. **It was a privilege to fight for public transit while serving on the MTC** After five meaningful years, I have stepped down from my role as a Commissioner with the Metropolitan Transportation Commission, and I’m grateful for the opportunity to have represented San Mateo County and our Board of Supervisors at the regional level. I was humbled to receive an honorary resolution by the Commission for my role as Chair of the Joint MTC ABAG Legislation Committee which played a pivotal role in the achievement of MTC’s top priority for the 2025 state legislative session by guiding development of the Connect Bay Area Act introduced as Senate Bill 63 by senators Scott Wiener and Jesse Arreguín. I was commended for continually urging a focus on improving the transit rider experience and helping to navigate its passage through the hearings-and-amendments process and floor votes in both the Senate and Assembly before the bill was signed into law by Gov. Gavin Newsom. From supporting Caltrain electrification and BART improvements in San Mateo County to expanding Bay Wheels in Daly City and advancing key regional upgrades, I worked to balance strong regional leadership with local advocacy. As I step away from MTC, I remain fully committed to serving our community, fighting for affordability, sustainability, opportunity and continuing this work both as a supervisor and a father. **M.P. Brown students get a lesson in civil liberties at 500 County Center** I had the honor of welcoming students from Margaret Pauline Brown Elementary recently to 500 County Center as we recognized Fred Korematsu Day of Civil Liberties and the Constitution. Seeing these young students from Daly City engage with this history right here in our halls of government is a powerful reminder of why Korematsu Day matters. Fred Korematsu stood up for his rights at a time when doing so came at great personal cost, and his courage ultimately helped expose a grave injustice and advance civil rights for generations to come. Korematsu Day is about more than remembering the past; it’s about teaching our kids the importance of speaking up, defending our Constitution, and standing against injustice wherever it appears. I’m grateful to our County Office of Education, the Court Community Outreach Committee and all our partners for creating meaningful, hands-on learning experiences that inspire students to become informed, engaged advocates for justice and equality. The future is brighter when our young people understand the power of their voices. **USF grad students look toward a future of public service** It was exciting to be back on the Hilltop at the beautiful University of San Francisco campus Tuesday night, Feb. 3, to sit down and engage in a lively discussion with my former Politics Professor Patrick Murphy, far left in the photo, and many of his current graduate students interested in pursuing a life of public service just as I’ve done since the day I graduated USF in 1998. Murphy is the faculty director for both the Masters of Urban and Public Affairs and Masters of Public Administration programs at USF and has inspired three decades of students to become future leaders. I shared a little about what a “day in the life” looks like serving on the San Mateo County Board of Supervisors this past 10 years, the choices and tradeoffs I’ve made along the way and what I’ve learned about persistence, public service and staying grounded in your values.

I’m always inspired by how thoughtful and engaged these students are. Their questions about leadership, decision-making and navigating public service in today’s challenging climate reminded me why it’s so important to invest in the next generation. Huge thanks Professor Murphy for the invitation and to the students for the energy and great conversation. I left encouraged about the future of public service. Go Dons!

**Interns wanted to join our team ** We are looking to add to our great group of interns we are currently working with. If you or someone you know may be interested in applying to my Internship Program, submitting this form is the first step: [https://forms.gle/hiKqtn7Rird5vXwB9](https://davidcanepa.us1.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c7592558e548bc8cc150aa5&id=f24d070237&e=c0babbc643 "https://forms.gle/hiKqtn7Rird5vXwB9?fbclid=IwAR3YFH0mH828rtAUru5EFOO9GsMCasQYe1N7AUrmwAwBf30JTtXOSeCzKjs"). You can also reach out to Mike Richardson on my staff directly with any questions at [mrichardson@smcgov.org](mailto:mrichardson@smcgov.org "mailto:mrichardson@smcgov.org"). In friendship,
**DAVID J. CANEPA**
President, San Mateo County Board of Supervisors

Brown students get a lesson in civil liberties at 500 County Center I had the honor of welcoming students from Margaret Pauline Brown Elementary recently to 500 County Center as we recognized Fred Korematsu Day of Civil Liberties and the Constitution. Seeing these young students from Daly City engage with this history right here in our halls of government is a powerful reminder of why Korematsu Day matters. Fred Korematsu stood up for his rights at a time when doing so came at great personal cost, and his courage ultimately helped expose a grave injustice and advance civil rights for generations to come. Korematsu Day is about more than remembering the past; it’s about teaching our kids the importance of speaking up, defending our Constitution, and standing against injustice wherever it appears. I’m grateful to our County Office of Education, the Court Community Outreach Committee and all our partners for creating meaningful, hands-on learning experiences that inspire students to become informed, engaged advocates for justice and equality. The future is brighter when our young people understand the power of their voices. USF grad students look toward a future of public service It was exciting to be back on the Hilltop at the beautiful University of San Francisco campus Tuesday night, Feb. 3, to sit down and engage in a lively discussion with my former Politics Professor Patrick Murphy, far left in the photo, and many of his current graduate students interested in pursuing a life of public service just as I’ve done since the day I graduated USF in 1998. Murphy is the faculty director for both the Masters of Urban and Public Affairs and Masters of Public Administration programs at USF and has inspired three decades of students to become future leaders. I shared a little about what a “day in the life” looks like serving on the San Mateo County Board of Supervisors this past 10 years, the choices and tradeoffs I’ve made along the way and what I’ve learned about persistence, public service and staying grounded in your values. I’m always inspired by how thoughtful and engaged these students are. Their questions about leadership, decision-making and navigating public service in today’s challenging climate reminded me why it’s so important to invest in the next generation. Huge thanks Professor Murphy for the invitation and to the students for the energy and great conversation. I left encouraged about the future of public service. Go Dons! Interns wanted to join our team We are looking to add to our great group of interns we are currently working with. If you or someone you know may be interested in applying to my Internship Program, submitting this form is the first step: "". You can also reach out to Mike Richardson on my staff directly with any questions at mailto:mrichardson@smcgov.org "mailto:mrichardson@smcgov.org". In friendship, DAVID J. _Mourning the Loss of Congressman Lee Hamilton_ [__](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124876957/599987545/-783470988?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDMvMS82NzYzNSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2MDhkOWNiNS1hMjAzLWYxMTEtODMyZi0wMDBkM2ExZjBlNGMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogIkRQV0lMTElTNjdAR01BSUwuQ09NIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=dXAqRtCQfsSCN9YUBrhIsyZwG3wCuQNW-T9HyP5hOV0=&emci=13d6a4a9-9e03-f111-832f-000d3a1f0e4c&emdi=608d9cb5-a203-f111-832f-000d3a1f0e4c&ceid=4925535) Hoosiers lost one of our greatest statesmen this week with the passing of former U.S. Congressman Lee Hamilton. Rep. Hamilton served the Ninth District of Indiana in the United States House from 1965 to 1999. Rep. Hamilton was lauded across the political spectrum for his ability to work across the aisle and bring results for Hoosiers. He helped shape American foreign policy during his 35 years in office, and always listened to his constituents. He also helped lead the 9/11 Commission and the Iraq Study Group after leaving Congress in the early 2000s. We’re grateful for his service to our state, and may we all learn from his legacy. ****_Nearly 60,000 Fewer Hoosiers Sign Up on Health Insurance Exchange_
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124876958/599987546/1463792004?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDMvMS82NzYzNSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2MDhkOWNiNS1hMjAzLWYxMTEtODMyZi0wMDBkM2ExZjBlNGMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogIkRQV0lMTElTNjdAR01BSUwuQ09NIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=dXAqRtCQfsSCN9YUBrhIsyZwG3wCuQNW-T9HyP5hOV0=&emci=13d6a4a9-9e03-f111-832f-000d3a1f0e4c&emdi=608d9cb5-a203-f111-832f-000d3a1f0e4c&ceid=4925535) Nearly 60,000 Hoosiers have lost healthcare coverage since the end of last year due to skyrocketing costs. At a time when Hoosiers were already struggling to keep up with costs, Republicans eliminated premium tax credits that these Hoosiers relied on. Every Indiana Republican in Congress supported this, and Jim Banks and Todd Young both refused to bring these subsidies to a vote in the U.S. Senate. Republicans are leading our state down a path of disaster. It’s time to elect new leadership this November that will restore these credits. ****_Each week, the State Party will highlight key policy from Democrats at the Statehouse or across the state. Democrats deliver a better future for Hoosier families, and we urge you to share this information with your networks._ [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124876959/599987547/1463792004?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDMvMS82NzYzNSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2MDhkOWNiNS1hMjAzLWYxMTEtODMyZi0wMDBkM2ExZjBlNGMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogIkRQV0lMTElTNjdAR01BSUwuQ09NIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=dXAqRtCQfsSCN9YUBrhIsyZwG3wCuQNW-T9HyP5hOV0=&emci=13d6a4a9-9e03-f111-832f-000d3a1f0e4c&emdi=608d9cb5-a203-f111-832f-000d3a1f0e4c&ceid=4925535) We are officially at the halfway point of the 2026 legislative session. While this is another session where Republicans have passed cruel and unnecessary legislation, there are also several glimmers of hope coming from our hardworking Statehouse Democrats. The new congressional map has changed the math in Virginia's 5th Congressional — and for the first time in decades, Democrats have a real opportunity to flip this seat.
I'm Mel Tull. I'm a Henrico-based business lawyer, Army veteran, and longtime leader in the Henrico Democratic Committee. I'm running because this newly competitive district needs a nominee who is deeply rooted in our community, understands how our economy actually works, and can unite suburban and rural Democrats to win in November.
But vulnerability doesn't equal victory. We need to show real momentum in the next 90 days to prove this is a competitive race and give Democratic voters a genuine choice in this primary.
I've spent 30 years helping businesses, workers, and communities navigate the real economy. I've served our party for years — including as Treasurer of the Henrico Democratic Committee — building something serious and sustainable. I know what it takes to organize, to win, and to actually deliver results once you're in office.
This race isn't about ideology. It's about who can bring together a changing district and actually win in November. It's about who has the roots, the experience, and the plan to flip a seat Republicans have held for decades.
From Henrico and the suburbs to rural communities across the new 5th District, I believe Democrats win by listening everywhere and governing competently. By focusing on what matters to families: lowering costs, protecting healthcare, and making government work for people again.
Republicans think redistricting won't matter. They think they're safe because this district has always been theirs.
They're wrong. BIG TIME!
We're at an inflection point. Redistricting has given us an opportunity we haven't had in a generation. Special elections across the country are showing Democrats have momentum. Our base is fired up and ready to fight.
But we need resources to capitalize on this moment. We need to build a campaign that can compete in every corner of this newly drawn district. We need to show donors, volunteers, and voters that this race is real and we're serious about winning it.
I'm asking you to consider a contribution of $25, $50, or $100 today to help us reach our next goal and keep this race competitive. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/melltull4congress]
DONATE TODAY TO HELP US WIN! >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/melltull4congress]
Thank you for everything you do for our party and our community.
Mel Tull

Democrat

body:
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124877406/599989097/-2000534896?amount=10&refcode=LOC_EM_FR_2026.02.06_Mark-Kelly-Split_B1_F1_S1_C1_90OP_N-T0&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODg1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1MTA2ZDc3MS1hNDAzLWYxMTEtODMyZi0wMDBkM2ExZjBlNGMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=m-ExB9CMLzgSjskbNmPomodN3RfS0nWWMQNrs73Kc0o=) Team, it's Mark.

Most of you probably know that I am suing the Secretary of Defense. Earlier this week I was in court to make my case against Pete Hegseth.

After 25 years in uniform and another 5 in the United States Senate, I never imagined I’d have to do something like that. Hegseth has left me no choice.

When he censured me and threatened my rank and retirement, he came after what I earned over 25 years — and chilled the free speech rights of every retired member of the military alongside me.

If Hegseth isn’t stopped, our longest-serving military veterans will have to live with the constant threat that they could be deprived of their rank and pension years — even decades — after they leave the military if they say something he doesn’t like.

I’m not going to sit by and let that happen. So, I sued Hegseth. And now, we wait and see what the court decides.

I’ve been truly humbled by the support people have sent my way over the past couple of months. It means the world to me that so many of you care about what Trump and Hegseth are trying to do.

That’s how we’ve made it this far, and it’s how we’ll get to the other side of this chapter in our nation’s history. Together.

If you’ve been waiting for the right time to make a stand and join the fight, this is it.

🔥 Our social coverage is catching fire. We’re pulling back the curtain on corruption at the Capitol and across Colorado—follow along so you don’t miss a thing:

**🏛️ Under the Golden Dome...** Lawmakers advanced proposals critics say expand state power, with the Senate moving to [widen Colorado’s red flag law](https://link.email.joinrmv.) by allowing schools and health providers to seek firearm seizures without prior notice, raising due-process concerns. At the same time, House Democrats introduced a [“captive customer” bill imposing price controls on certain businesses](https://link.email.joinrmv.), prompting warnings about government overreach into private markets.
🏔️ **Here in Colorado...** Accountability and rising costs dominated the week as the Department of Agriculture moved to dismiss a [DEI-related whistleblower complaint](https://link.email.joinrmv.), while Rep. Lauren Boebert secured nearly $15 million for rural water and infrastructure. A Greeley-Evans school nurse was [reprimanded over an anti-ICE email](https://link.email.joinrmv.), an RTD panel called for [structural reforms amid declining ridership](https://link.email.joinrmv.), regulators [approved Xcel’s renewable buildout](https://link.email.joinrmv.) despite cost concerns, and and Attorney General [Phil Weiser’s taxpayer-funded ICE reporting portal](https://link.email.joinrmv.) has become a flashpoint in Colorado’s broader political and public safety debate.
🇺🇸**On the National Stage...** National debates sharpened as House Republicans forced a [vote on citizenship and photo ID requirements for voters](https://link.email.joinrmv.), setting up a defining election integrity fight. Meanwhile, parents across the country raised alarms over [reports of teachers pushing anti-ICE activism on young students](https://link.email.joinrmv.), intensifying concerns about political ideology in classrooms.
This is your Mountain Minute for Friday, February 6, 2026.
– Team RMV

**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[Phil Weiser’s ICE portal: A hotline for the wrong crisis](https://link.email.joinrmv.)** BY RMV EDITORIAL BOARD, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
[](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
_Colorado Attorney General Phil Weiser wants you to do something. Not vote. Not volunteer. Not show up to a school board meeting and read the agenda before somebody else reads it for you.**He wants you to report ICE.**_
_Weiser’s office rolled out a portal inviting Coloradans to document “concerns” about Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents. His pitch is tidy and familiar. The public assumes rules apply to everyone and that safety isn’t optional. When that assumption fails, there needs to be a way to say so. Fine. In theory._
_In practice, this portal is a neon sign pointing at the wrong problem. It’s a taxpayer-funded invitation to fixate on federal immigration enforcement while the crimes and dysfunction Coloradans actually live with keep stacking up. It’s also a political instrument that makes a lot more sense when you place it in the larger fight Colorado is already waging against ICE._
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.joinrmv.)**
|

**[Colorado Senate moves to widen red flag authority despite due process warnings](https://link.email.joinrmv.)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
* **Senate expands red flag authority despite due-process warnings:** SB26-004 passed the Colorado Senate on a 20–13 vote, widening who can petition for firearm seizures to include schools and health-care institutions, allowing guns to be taken through civil orders issued without prior notice to the accused.

* **Firearms can be seized before a person is notified or heard:** The bill preserves ex parte hearings, meaning a judge may order removal based on one-sided claims, with the individual only allowed to challenge the seizure after it has already occurred.

* **No penalties for false or reckless filings raise abuse concerns:** While SB26-004 grants broad immunity to petitioners and investigators, it includes no safeguards, audits, or consequences for malicious or unfounded petitions, prompting warnings that lawful gun owners have little recourse.

**[Colorado ag department seeks dismissal of whistleblower complaint over DEI as employee calls for HR director removal](https://link.email.joinrmv.)** BY JEN SCHUMANN, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
* **State agriculture department moves to dismiss DEI whistleblower complaint:** The Colorado Department of Agriculture is asking an administrative judge to throw out a whistleblower claim alleging retaliation after an employee raised concerns about internal DEI practices and hiring decisions.
* **Employee alleges retaliation and calls for HR director’s removal:** The complainant argues the department ignored procedural safeguards and retaliated against him after he questioned DEI-driven workplace actions, formally requesting the removal of the agency’s human resources director.
* **Case raises broader questions about transparency and accountability:** The dispute highlights growing tensions inside state agencies over DEI implementation, employee protections, and whether whistleblower laws are being enforced—or avoided—when complaints challenge ideological priorities

[**Do We Vote by Faith in Colorado?**](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
[****](https://link.email.joinrmv.)**BY PAMELA POLL | COMMENTARY | FEBRUARY 6** _Former Mesa County Clerk Tina Peters has become a national figure in the battle for transparent elections in the USA. I believe her story holds important revelations. After the controversial 2020 election, around mid-year 2021, Colorado Secretary of State Jena Griswold informed County Clerks that an update of their Dominion election software called the ‘Trusted Build’ would be installed on their election server. Preserving election data for at least 22 months is required by Federal law._

[**Parents allege school mistreatment of autistic child as Cherry Creek faces federal civil rights investigation**](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
[****](https://link.email.joinrmv.)**BY SHAINA COLE | LOCAL | FEBRUARY 4** _In response to concerns raised by a family in Colorado about the treatment of their young son in kindergarten, the Office for Civil Rights of the U.S. Department of Education opened an investigation into whether the Cherry Creek School District was in compliance with federal civil rights and special education law, a problem that is not new to the district._

[****](https://link.email.joinrmv.)**BY JEN SCHUMANN | LOCAL | FEBRUARY 3** _“There’s a lot of candidates running and I know there’s a lot of confusion out there about who conservatives in the area should be supporting,” said James Ruehmann, president of the Turning Point USA chapter at CMU._

Peter,
Speaker Johnson just revealed plans to tack the SAVE Act — one of the most extreme anti-voter bills in recent history — on to funding for the Department of Homeland Security. They’re going to try to pass this without needing to reach the 60-vote threshold in the Senate.
These guys think voters aren’t paying attention. [**Let’s show them they’re dead wrong — send an urgent message to Congress right now and tell them to stop the SAVE Act.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124878733/599993701/-2121636071?refcode=eng_aotl_tier1_email_SaveActKicker_email_20260206-AOTL-Tier1-SaveActKicker_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=eng&utm_content=20260206-AOTL-Tier1-SaveActKicker_&utm_campaign=SaveActKicker&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk2IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjAyYmMwNzQwLWE3MDMtZjExMS04MzJmLTAwMGQzYTFmMGU0YyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=P4gHnp-x_FYY3rDWcsf8cw1f8yUStpzoMcmn8v4rljc=&emci=b8dd99b9-8303-f111-832f-000d3a1f0e4c&emdi=02bc0740-a703-f111-832f-000d3a1f0e4c&ceid=8431045)
If you don’t remember our fight to defeat the SAVE Act last year, this bill is designed to create barriers that would make it harder for millions of Americans to vote — all in the name of a voter fraud crisis that simply doesn’t exist.
Here’s who could be affected:
* Married women who have changed their last names and don’t have a birth certificate with their current legal name.
* Military voters who will no longer be able to use their military ID to register.
* Americans who don’t have a passport, who are more likely to come from lower-income families.
* Transgender Americans who have changed their legal names.
* Rural voters who often rely on online and mail-in voter registration.
* People who have lost documents to natural disasters, and so many more.

The House narrowly passed the SAVE Act last year but the Senate didn’t have the votes to take it up. With President Trump calling for the federal government to “take over” elections this week, it’s no wonder that anti-democracy lawmakers are trying again.
They know they need to stoop to sneaky maneuvers to pass this unpopular bill. As Senate Majority Leader John Thune said, “Any legislative vehicle that crosses the floor could be a candidate for an amendment vote.”
**If the SAVE Act becomes law, millions of Americans will have a harder time casting a ballot — that’s as anti-democracy as it gets.[Now is an urgent time to speak out and tell your senator to vote down the SAVE Act.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124878734/599993702/-2121636071?refcode=eng_aotl_tier1_email_SaveActKicker_email_20260206-AOTL-Tier1-SaveActKicker_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=eng&utm_content=20260206-AOTL-Tier1-SaveActKicker_&utm_campaign=SaveActKicker&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk2IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjAyYmMwNzQwLWE3MDMtZjExMS04MzJmLTAwMGQzYTFmMGU0YyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=P4gHnp-x_FYY3rDWcsf8cw1f8yUStpzoMcmn8v4rljc=&emci=b8dd99b9-8303-f111-832f-000d3a1f0e4c&emdi=02bc0740-a703-f111-832f-000d3a1f0e4c&ceid=8431045)**

clean_body: Lawmakers are trying to sneak this extreme anti-voter legislation through. Act now. | Peter, First, we helped stop the SAVE Act last year, where it stalled because it didn’t have enough votes to overcome a Senate filibuster. Now, under pressure from the White House to “take over” elections, some lawmakers have come up with a scheme to pass it anyway — sneaking it into a funding bill. This is an all-hands-on-deck moment. Millions of Americans could have their registration threatened or invalidated if this legislation passes — Thank you — we’ll keep you posted on the latest. \- The Redistricting Action team \--------- Forwarded email --------- Peter, Speaker Johnson just revealed plans to tack the SAVE Act — one of the most extreme anti-voter bills in recent history — on to funding for the Department of Homeland Security. They’re going to try to pass this without needing to reach the 60-vote threshold in the Senate. These guys think voters aren’t paying attention. If you don’t remember our fight to defeat the SAVE Act last year, this bill is designed to create barriers that would make it harder for millions of Americans to vote — all in the name of a voter fraud crisis that simply doesn’t exist. Here’s who could be affected: Married women who have changed their last names and don’t have a birth certificate with their current legal name. Military voters who will no longer be able to use their military ID to register. Americans who don’t have a passport, who are more likely to come from lower-income families. Transgender Americans who have changed their legal names. Rural voters who often rely on online and mail-in voter registration. People who have lost documents to natural disasters, and so many more. The House narrowly passed the SAVE Act last year but the Senate didn’t have the votes to take it up. With President Trump calling for the federal government to “take over” elections this week, it’s no wonder that anti-democracy lawmakers are trying again. They know they need to stoop to sneaky maneuvers to pass this unpopular bill. As Senate Majority Leader John Thune said, “Any legislative vehicle that crosses the floor could be a candidate for an amendment vote.” If the SAVE Act becomes law, millions of Americans will have a harder time casting a ballot — that’s as anti-democracy as it gets. # [](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/35?t=1&akid=2073%2E791427%2Ew4BWkZ)
Friend, last week I told you about this incident, which occurred in Maine:
[](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/4863?t=2&akid=2073%2E791427%2Ew4BWkZ)
This is not an isolated incident either. ICE is telling people who are practicing their Constitutional rights from Maine to Minnesota that they are “domestic terrorists” and putting them in a federal database.
We’ve heard this term used before. Alex Pretti and Renee Good were called domestic terrorists by Kristi Noem and DHS, a disgusting and outlandish slander meant to justify the murder of two innocent people.
By slapping the “domestic terrorist” label on any legal observer, organizer, or protester, ICE has allowed itself to gather tons of data and act as Big Brother:
[](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/4881?t=3&akid=2073%2E791427%2Ew4BWkZ)
Through databases, facial recognition technology, and social media monitoring, DHS and ICE are tracking anyone who disagrees with them. They are sweeping photos, license plates, and personal data into these databases to create full profiles of US citizens who are simply practicing their rights. **It’s completely unacceptable, and most likely illegal.**
We are watching our government create a mass surveillance system to track its political enemies, in collaboration with Trump’s Big Tech billionaire buddies. Their goal is to intimidate us and put a chilling effect on the entire First Amendment.
So here’s my message to anyone who is observing, tracking, documenting, or peacefully protesting ICE: You are certainly not a domestic terrorist. You are an American patriot, upholding our Constitutional traditions and putting to practice the sacred freedoms that make America great.
They are surveilling us because they are scared. Because this administration is weak. Because the thing they fear the most is regular folks organizing to topple their fascist occupation.
They can call us domestic terrorists all they want — the only terror I see is the daily brutality, fear, and chaos unleashed by ICE in my district and my state.
**Friend — It is our patriotic duty to continue to fight back, regardless of what this corrupt, authoritarian administration throws at us. They want to play Big Brother, but their intimidation and scare tactics will not deter us.**

I want to level with you for a moment, because what just happened in Texas should concern every Republican who cares about keeping this country on track.

A legislative seat that Republicans have held for decades just flipped to the Democrats in a special election. This is the kind of district our party normally wins comfortably. The kind of district that never makes national headlines because the outcome is supposed to be predictable. And yet, Democrats just walked away with it.

That is not a coincidence. And it is not something we can brush off.

[**SAVE THE GOP MAJORITY**](http://links.conservativesdefendingfreedom.com/u/click?_t=91d01aa68bbe4105984439520ca0f0af&_m=81c022e78f34418b8de31851fc03c5d2&_e=1zNw6236waVrSE7S5byI4cYG2oQL816uIvLkW70rWSlC1cMuJ375vN81bEe4KjlxjdksNBO6xTrxApPHJXjzSExt54nUO6Eax6fvnAv_WpGufQts5tmF8bpvpEnHyyzoP27u0YMgYbnRJLpW_gxfXEt7T4CvaJvBmKhhLGC0IQHJkTPK3Az6HcUZYoxq39EK03dbJQekMsoMLGbJ47U1cycvglzKFSUunnYdCEN1a6WyXAXb4a9J9yBzKUFPBEA59GAiT-6lsNgPO8LaZKoXeanySVm0BLYSiX2jWizNVaQN5CoUS2hiaNxfT5F8iF9_YIxd4Uo5LV1cAxzJ_FFAktI_P8__drkNxwbDvoVPMMn8mH1GSD9mGFz3l7CBW7n2LcoHayWNFbd8-_z3zi98xocUPt37v743deT88oVwV82b5FujRR4d44IaPJEISMI_sMHMxgSu4-Wwelubr2Wnw3b2BpK0w_UC6vcueFf4iQ43t7HoR-dxwRkrQ9U0-xi3Cb3nqyZf8gNfH1Slm-HqM5KoQYc6QQU4MnM-fqPZixqmwRIcbGS7JMtI6qQIFxAu2tvAF3njvcK63mUWldJSSjoM-udkMoNpcKfhbFfjQQEG62oFZTNHx0zz479mZ1usXUEdpx6GNDszsnuNCV3zCHWkCV2ZMuKsK6NvGpyqV5rDbxO27Iw3sWN0tA7Jp5aJx8w7TCNmDAScUwQ3ZHHDkYZYIUBlp3ZQDbNHJwqt3WY%3D)
**Special elections are always imperfect snapshots, but they are often the earliest warning signs of the political climate heading into a midterm year.** When voters start drifting away from us in places we normally dominate, it tells us enthusiasm is uneven, turnout is fragile, and Democrats are doing a better job motivating their base than we are motivating ours.

They believe momentum is on their side, and they intend to nationalize every competitive race, including districts like mine.

If they succeed, we are looking at a House run by Hakeem Jeffries, endless investigations designed to cripple and IMPEACH President Trump, and a radical legislative agenda that raises taxes, stops border enforcement, and blocks every serious reform Republicans are trying to pass.

_I refuse to accept that future._

That is why my campaign is acting early. We are building our turnout and digital programs now, reserving resources now, and preparing to communicate aggressively with voters long before Democrats define the battlefield for us.

But early action requires early support.

clean_body: Special elections are always imperfect snapshots, but they are often the earliest warning signs of the political climate heading into a midterm year. | Fellow American — I want to level with you for a moment, because what just happened in Texas should concern every Republican who cares about keeping this country on track. A legislative seat that Republicans have held for decades just flipped to the Democrats in a special election. This is the kind of district our party normally wins comfortably. The kind of district that never makes national headlines because the outcome is supposed to be predictable. And yet, Democrats just walked away with it. That is not a coincidence. And it is not something we can brush off. Special elections are always imperfect snapshots, but they are often the earliest warning signs of the political climate heading into a midterm year. When voters start drifting away from us in places we normally dominate, it tells us enthusiasm is uneven, turnout is fragile, and Democrats are doing a better job motivating their base than we are motivating ours. Democrats are openly talking about taking back the gavel in 2026. They are recruiting candidates, lining up donors, and building massive outside spending operations right now. They believe momentum is on their side, and they intend to nationalize every competitive race, including districts like mine. If they succeed, we are looking at a House run by Hakeem Jeffries, endless investigations designed to cripple and IMPEACH President Trump, and a radical legislative agenda that raises taxes, stops border enforcement, and blocks every serious reform Republicans are trying to pass. I refuse to accept that future. That is why my campaign is acting early. We are building our turnout and digital programs now, reserving resources now, and preparing to communicate aggressively with voters long before Democrats define the battlefield for us. But early action requires early support. This Texas flip was a warning. What we do next will determine whether it stays a warning, or becomes the beginning of something much worse. Beth Van Duyne Congresswoman (TX-24) P.S. Complacency is how majorities die. Urgency is how they’re saved. | | PAID FOR BY BETH VAN DUYNE FOR CONGRESS

Offering some perspective |
#
---

He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal.
