Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. [ stdin# ]Jocelyn Benson for Governor
Hi, I know you get a lot of emails from me. So I wanted to
take a step back and tell you a little bit more about me and why I’m
running to be the next Governor of Michigan.

Ever since I was a student, I knew I wanted to fight for justice and make
a difference. I’m the daughter of two special education teachers. I was
raised in a working class family that instilled in me the values of hard
work, opportunity, and serving others.

It’s why I started my career investigating threats to democracy and civil
rights in the US and abroad.

It’s why I became a law clerk in Detroit, fighting to protect and defend
people’s civil rights and freedoms.

It’s why as Dean of Wayne State University Law School, I worked to ensure
all students could afford their education, froze tuition, and expanded
scholarships.

And it’s why as Secretary of State, I’ve fought to make everyday life
easier for all Michiganders, secure our elections, and expand voter
access.

But I know our work is far from finished. So now, I’m running for Governor
to make sure Michigan is a place where everyone – from our kids to our
seniors – can stay and thrive.

I know that government works best when it’s there when you need it, and
gets out of the way when you don’t. So here’s my promise to you: when we
win this election, I will use every tool available to make life easier:
expand rural healthcare options, build more housing, take on the utility
companies who raise our rates, make childcare free, and ensure anyone can
afford to live in the best place to call home.

But here’s the truth: Michigan is one of the most competitive states in
the entire country, and our opponents have the backing of big billionaires
and special interests. I can only win this race with your support, so
today, I’m asking:

This week’s
judicial hearings were a sham.

Trump’s nominees were handed the softest possible test — questions about
reality: Who won the 2020 election? Was January 6 an attack on the U.S.
Capitol?

These nominees chose to avoid historical fact and hide behind rehearsed
non-answers and legal wordplay — dodging any answer that might upset
Trump.

Senator Richard Blumenthal called it what it was:

“I am insulted as a member of this body that you won’t tell us the truth...
You’ve all been carefully rehearsed... I think you failed the test.”

He’s right. They failed — deliberately.

These nominees are demonstrating loyalty. They’re signaling that they’ll
protect Trump’s lies, excuse political violence, and stay silent when
democracy is attacked, all in exchange for a lifetime seat on the bench.

And here’s the most enraging part... Nineteen Senate Democrats have voted to
confirm these judges.

Nineteen. Let that sink in.

And every vote “yes” helps pack the courts with Trump cronies — judges who
won’t defend elections, won’t condemn insurrection, and won’t protect our
rights when it counts.

Demand Justice PAC is done pretending this is normal. We’re calling out

Peter,

I have some exciting news to share.

Common Defense — a national grassroots organization of more than 500,000
veterans and military families — just endorsed our campaign for U.S.
Senate.

This endorsement isn’t about politics-as-usual. It’s about trust.

Veterans know what it means to serve, to sacrifice, and to expect leaders
to keep their word.

Common Defense is backing our campaign because they know I’ll fight for
guaranteed healthcare, a strong VA, an economy that respects hard work,
and a government that actually keeps its promises.

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260206-2-ak.EOLH1b&amount=10&refcode=em20260206-1658&t=1004&akid=1663%2E251025%2EAQ8fGx ]If you share those values, make a split donation today to support our
campaign and Common Defense so that we can continue building a movement
that honors service with action and delivers for working people across
Michigan.

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260206-2-ak.EOLH1b&amount=10&refcode=em20260206-1658&t=1023&akid=1663%2E251025%2EAQ8fGx ]Donate $10 ››

Peter, before
launching this campaign, I served as director of the Department of Health,
Human, and Veterans Services for Wayne County.

I worked directly with veterans facing eviction, foreclosure, crushing
medical bills, and impossible bureaucracy. We helped folks get the care
they’d earned.

We showed that government can deliver when it’s focused on people instead
of profits.

Veterans are standing behind that kind of leadership because they know it
delivers results. But endorsements alone won’t win this Senate race.
People power will.

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260206-2-ak.EOLH1b&amount=10&refcode=em20260206-1658&t=1024&akid=1663%2E251025%2EAQ8fGx ]That’s why I’m hoping you’ll donate $10 today, split
between our campaign and Common Defense. Your contribution helps elect
leaders who take service seriously and strengthens the movement pushing
our government to live up to its obligations.

Your friend in the fight,

Abdul

**– Chelsie’s note –**
Peter,
I’m the president of Minneapolis Regional Labor Federation, and my city is under occupation by the federal government.
During this crisis, our community has pulled together, blowing whistles, following ICE vehicles, and doing everything we can to protect our neighbors from being kidnapped and detained by ICE and border patrol.
**February is here, and the rent is due.** And that’s a problem for our neighbors.
**Imagine this happening to you:**
One of our members was detained by ICE in the parking lot of their workplace, where they were swept away to a facility in Texas. After two weeks in detention under astonishing conditions, being pressured to sign “voluntary” deportation orders, the worker was finally granted habeas and was released.
Two other children in the household also work at the workplace where the detainment took place. It is not safe to return to work―so they have had no income for weeks. They are thankful to be reunited, but afraid that eviction is around the corner. **There are more stories like this than you can believe. These are the families we are supporting with rent.**
[**Minneapolis Regional Labor Federation created a fund to pay the rent for families who can’t go to work because they are threatened by ICE. Our movement is built on the combined strength of $5 and $10 donations. When everyone gives a little, they go a long way. Can you split a donation to protect our neighbors?**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqvd8hCserj-XmGYLB0-0IMX1om1J0_1aEV2b-kAgyJHHsXtq8k5iY8bvzDBsWY97Upla4jHhuvWYriDS1RB8_MtXSvVGmlKes-3eqDn2T2Iwu20PxGvTDXIxrCh5c7tSmTG2kY_kKSgUa0DWmomiBs3CBQsjt0B4JA3xGTxOAWrst9eoKPTssIOfg-VzR8HJM6KEQwSrUrIxWHHuOQb-Kf8xSYXq7UL4e6wXqoc6jQWBVJuqYxu40oPW3ennWm8C4jPv_jD751CDsmDuC0GMJvia5fhzAWWVpuYJDf1k3qmKy_naSVvPiTMmOj0TyoVS_9FYOVT2KwgJ2vnDlhuttBG1PWcjBbm4jnK2dzK2SUofA/4nx/9vDI-tyaSimcsl_nRl2DYw/h7/h001.FoXG-ir3k_V_NqSkHBDuAGe-ELmVaZ4AYHkky5ZvM4U)
One thing I’ve learned in this process is that it’s _difficult_ to pay someone else’s rent. Not any organization can do it. But we can. Our navigators help renters get in touch with leasing companies and landlords, and keep people in their homes.
We’ve called for an eviction pause during this emergency, but the government moves slowly and the crisis is now.
**If we don’t hit our goals:**
Landlords will begin eviction proceedings, potentially bringing law enforcement to the people who have successfully avoided ICE during the occupation.
We will keep fighting for our neighbors until ICE drags them to a country where we can't reach them. But the fastest, most effective protection we can give is if we can just pay their rent today.
[**Protect our neighbors! Help Minnesota residents targeted by ICE pay rent and avoid eviction this month.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqvd8hCserj-XmGYLB0-0IMX1om1J0_1aEV2b-kAgyJHHsXtq8k5iY8bvzDBsWY97Upla4jHhuvWYriDS1RB8_Mt_qpwxuzhEwskI5hpRByxgaGBOKymfWkY59mdCq-YafchDrAFd4EDxzFXI_3m3fHxW2uzexWGcOjAJ1Z9eVDTq7OjAWXUPpAX8W-UzgcOv3r8Fa-iTowqXJFA3dr65aDx-gmPwfLElGMeoGRw-WU-djWbcx-xT_B2o7Jtlrs8zA0X635P4ODFrc5h7xk4AGj3QpIijEXZVKlIiiuQVKxxS6PjUTYqCQTPqqiAuoFOD-r3PVegSUo20_ZB31N-FefcZuvX2uFhvcDtXVVWtfZzuw/4nx/9vDI-tyaSimcsl_nRl2DYw/h8/h001.CMm5YNBtf0S7vFoiDxWleruyz75dh3_3Ve1n4SolbLM)
The labor movement is built on solidarity. When people stand together, we are more powerful than any other force. Thank you to United for Democracy for standing with us.
In solidarity,
Chelsie Glaubitz Gabiou
_President, Minneapolis Regional Labor Federation_

| Hi Peter,

Inauguration weekend was an unforgettable one for me and my family.

Being sworn in as Governor of Virginia was a moment of deep gratitude and reflection — made even more special by the people who joined us to celebrate, and by the knowledge of how many Virginians helped make this possible. From the ceremony itself to the quiet moments in between, I felt the weight of the responsibility and the optimism of what lies ahead.

I wanted to share a few photos from the weekend with you, because this milestone belongs to all of us. And even as we celebrate, the work is already underway. With the General Assembly now in session, I’m focused on turning the priorities we ran on into action — lowering costs for families, strengthening public schools, and making Virginia safer and more affordable for everyone. Thank you for believing in this work and for being part of this journey.
---
_The moment I was sworn in with my husband, Adam, and our daughters by my side._
_Delivering my inaugural speech to the crowd after being sworn in as Virginia’s 75th Governor._
_The crowd on inauguration day, braving the cold weather!_
_Celebrating with my family and friends at the inaugural ball._
With gratitude,

Abigail

Peter,
**Last night the progressive movement proved we have the momentum when Analilia Mejia surged into the lead in New Jersey’s Democratic primary for Congress:**
[](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260206.uBd6i8&refcode=em20260206-5890&t=2&akid=5890%2E420207%2EV2ITd3)
Despite being outspent by _millions_ by super PACs supporting her opponent, Analilia proved that when there’s a real organizer running, we don’t need to match the billionaires dollar for dollar — **we just need to be in the ring.**
In the closing four days of the primary, the Congressional Progressive Caucus PAC and my Medicare For All PAC moved **$100,000** in advertising dollars to support Analilia’s campaign because we know she’s exactly the kind of leader we need right now.
Her progress, her support, the numbers coming out of her race — show the growing wave of support for candidates who will never fold to Trump, MAGA extremists, or corporate special interests. The midterms are starting and our people power is growing.
This November, it’s not enough to eke out a slim Democratic majority. We need to make sure the midterms usher in a wave of change all over the country — with a blue wave that takes back the House _and_ a progressive wave that transforms the Democratic Party into a force that stands up to the billionaires and fights for working people.

subject: Honoring the past, facing the truth.
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY BELL FOR MISSOURI
body:
Happy Black History Month! **Happy Black History Month, Peter!**

Black History Month is about more than honoring the past. It's about telling the truth about where we've been, what we've survived, and what's being asked of us right now.

Black Americans have always been on the frontlines of building this country and pushing it to live up to its promise. From the courthouse to the Capitol, from the pulpit to the picket line, Black leaders and Black communities have led the fight for justice, dignity, and equal protection under the law.

Missouri's history is filled with that leadership...and so is its present. But right now, we need to be honest with ourselves, Peter. Across the country, we are seeing renewed racial targeting and intimidation. Families are living in fear, communities are being singled out, and enforcement systems are being used in ways that echo some of the darkest chapters of our history.

When immigration enforcement is weaponized through racial profiling, and when people are targeted because of how they look or where they come from, it undermines the very idea of justice. This administration is sending us a message that it believes our rights to be expendable. But Black History Month reminds us that our ancestors **never** asked for permission before demanding our rights be recognized and our voices heard.

Every gain — _from voting rights to civil rights to basic dignity_ — was fought for, protected, and defended by ordinary people who refused to look away when injustice showed up at their door. **That legacy belongs to us now, and this work continues in classrooms where history must be told honestly, in courtrooms where fairness must be demanded, and in neighborhoods where safety should never come at the cost of someone else's humanity.**

This month, and every month, let's honor the ancestors who pushed this country forward and recommit ourselves to carrying that responsibility forward.

Onward,

clean_body: Happy Black History Month! Happy Black History Month, Peter! Black History Month is about more than honoring the past. It's about telling the truth about where we've been, what we've survived, and what's being asked of us right now. Black Americans have always been on the frontlines of building this country and pushing it to live up to its promise. From the courthouse to the Capitol, from the pulpit to the picket line, Black leaders and Black communities have led the fight for justice, dignity, and equal protection under the law. Missouri's history is filled with that leadership...and so is its present. But right now, we need to be honest with ourselves, Peter. Across the country, we are seeing renewed racial targeting and intimidation. Families are living in fear, communities are being singled out, and enforcement systems are being used in ways that echo some of the darkest chapters of our history. When immigration enforcement is weaponized through racial profiling, and when people are targeted because of how they look or where they come from, it undermines the very idea of justice. This administration is sending us a message that it believes our rights to be expendable. But Black History Month reminds us that our ancestors never asked for permission before demanding our rights be recognized and our voices heard. Every gain — from voting rights to civil rights to basic dignity — was fought for, protected, and defended by ordinary people who refused to look away when injustice showed up at their door. That legacy belongs to us now, and this work continues in classrooms where history must be told honestly, in courtrooms where fairness must be demanded, and in neighborhoods where safety should never come at the cost of someone else's humanity. This month, and every month, let's honor the ancestors who pushed this country forward and recommit ourselves to carrying that responsibility forward. Onward, Wesley | = = PAID FOR BY BELL FOR MISSOURI PO Box 190669, ST LOUIS, MO 63119

Peter,
Zohran Mamdani has wrapped up his first month as mayor of New York City, and what he’s accomplishing shouldn’t surprise you.
_This is what happens when Leaders We Deserve candidates get elected and prioritize everyday people, not special interests._
**[Peter, if you want to see more leaders like Zohran delivering real change in their first month in office, contribute $5 to Leaders We Deserve today.](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260206_1_zohran.G7gPHA&refcode=em20260206-3126&amount=5&t=2&akid=3126%2E587540%2EaKCfyn)**

In one month, Mamdani has:
**Helped make housing affordable.** He revived the Office to Protect Tenants that Eric Adams gutted. Launched task forces to eliminate barriers and fast-track affordable housing on city-owned land. And started "Rental Ripoff" hearings across all five boroughs so New Yorkers can testify about abusive landlord practices.
**Delivered universal childcare.** He partnered with Governor Hochul to announce free childcare for 2-year-olds and expanded 3K and Pre-K programs.
**Made transit work.** He personally went out and fixed a dangerous bike lane bump on the Williamsburg Bridge himself because that's the kind of thing that actually matters to people trying to get to work safely.
**Cut the bullshit.** On day one, he revoked every executive order Eric Adams issued after his indictment. He mandated that every city agency appoint a "Chief Savings Officer" to eliminate waste. He cracked down on hidden fees in gym memberships and concert tickets.
It’s not that Mamdani is some kind of savant or genius. Someone with better policies who prioritizes normal people instead of the wealthy and well connected was elected instead of another establishment Dem catering to donors.
Mamdani is proving exactly why we started Leaders We Deserve — to elect leaders who don't just talk about change, but actually deliver it.
I’ve said this before about him: **When a candidate truly believes in what they’re saying and doesn’t change their values under pressure, that inspires people.** This New York race felt huge for so many young people across the nation, because they felt they could be part of the change.
_That’s how we win._ Without compromise.

_Peter_ __,_ this is Mazie. Below is a message from my colleague Sen. Jon Ossoff, who is running for re-election in Georgia. Please read his message below._
* * *
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124882046/600001993/1252725352?refcode=AU_MKH_FR_TAN_GEN_AC_20260206_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDUvMS83MTU3NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxMWNjOWM5Yy1hZjAzLWYxMTEtODMyZi0wMDBkM2ExZjBlNGMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=IvyC3Pa3-3lv2C_0lDlUwz1P0o5Bff-SoQbOr1QzkYQ=) See, I get why some folks voted for Trump. He promised to attack a broken system. And it’s a ripe target. Even before Trump came on the scene, America had one of the most corrupt political systems in the Western world. It’s been running on corporate money, secret money, billionaire money. And it’s worse than ever now. Citizens United was the worst court decision in modern American history. When Members of Congress aren’t begging for money from Washington lobbyists, they’re trying to dodge getting carpet-bombed by super PACs. Senators get threatened with millions of dollars of attack ads over the votes they take. And see, that is why things don’t work for ordinary people. It’s because the people’s elected representatives don’t represent the people. They represent the big donors! That corruption is why they defunded nursing homes to cut taxes for the rich. Corruption is why you pay a fortune for prescriptions. Corruption is why your insurance claim keeps getting denied. Corruption is why hedge funds get to buy up all the houses in your neighborhood, and then your corporate landlord ignores your calls during a gas leak. Corruption is why that ambulance costs $3,000 after you just had to get your choking toddler to the hospital. Yes, the system really is rigged. But Trump’s not unrigging it. He’s re-rigging it for himself! He’s a crook and a con man, and he wants to be a king. You can’t claim to be for ordinary men and women when you defund their hospitals and nursing homes. You can’t claim to be for ordinary men and women when you defund school lunch programs to help feed little boys and little girls whose hard-working parents are struggling to fill the fridge. You can’t claim to be for ordinary men and women when you do these things so you can cut taxes for the richest people in the country while you and your family business rake in massive sums from around the world. Donald Trump’s second term has already done unfathomable damage to our country and the lives of millions of people. And the people are beginning to see it. But only by regaining Congressional power can we stop him. Really. The upcoming 2026 midterms are our last chance to restore checks and balances. And my Senate race in Georgia is the single most critical contest: I’m the only Democratic Senator up for reelection in 2026 in a state Trump carried in 2024. So if you’re outraged by what’s happening to our country — and you’re ready to fight for the future of this Republic –– please don’t wait until 2028: Split a donation of $10 between Mazie Hirono and my reelection campaign in Georgia right now. name: Amy Klobuchar (via Elizabeth Warren)
subject: I want to be a transformative governor for the state of Minnesota.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Warren for Senate
body:
To accomplish everything we’re setting out to do, I need your support.

| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=2759%2E4032634%2EFX7sbF)
---
Hi there, I’m running for governor of the state of Minnesota. **This is a home-grown campaign, born in a moment like no other.** [**I’m going to tell you why in a moment. But first: Will you help us get off to a strong start by splitting a donation between Elizabeth Warren and my campaign?**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/3453?t=8&akid=2759%2E4032634%2EFX7sbF) I’m not going to sugar coat it -- Minnesota has been through a lot. The killings of two innocent Minnesotans. Three thousand ICE agents on our streets and in our towns, sent by an administration that relishes division. Minnesotans stood up. Our state has been the center of America’s heartbreak. But we have also been the center of America's courage and America's hope. In moments of enormous difficulty, we find strength in our Minnesota values of hard work, freedom, and simple decency and good will. **These moments call for grit and resilience.** I’ve learned resilience from the people of Minnesota. They have stood up, they have marched, and they have brought food to their neighbors. Through it all we do not give up. And grit? I learned that from my family. I’m the daughter of a newspaperman and a proud union member teacher. My grandpa worked 1500 feet underground in the mines on the Iron Range, and he saved his money in a coffee can in the basement to send my dad to college. I wouldn’t be where I am today without them. **These times call for leaders who can stand up and not be rubber stamps of this administration.** But who are also willing to find common ground and fix things in our state. I led our state’s biggest prosecutors’ office for eight years and then you gave me the honor of serving as your United States Senator. I was ranked number one in the Senate for bipartisan bills and number three out of one hundred for getting bills passed into law. **I will do my job without fear or favor. I’ve never shied away from taking on the powerful. That’s what I did as a prosecutor. That’s what I did as senator. And that’s what I will do as governor.** I believe we must stand up for what’s right. And fix what’s wrong. I am running for every Minnesotan who wants to buy their first home, for every parent who wants a better world for their kids, for everyone who wants more affordable healthcare. I am running for every Minnesotan who wants to protect our democracy and get ICE and its abusive tactics out of the state we love. And I'm running for every student, farmer, dreamer and builder. _But to accomplish everything we’re setting out to do, I need your support._ **This campaign is for people who believe in something bigger than ourselves. For people who know that things have got to change.** [**So please: Will you support my campaign for governor with a donation today? Your contribution will be split with Elizabeth Warren.**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/3453?t=9&akid=2759%2E4032634%2EFX7sbF) **I like my job in the Senate. But I love our state more than any job.** I love the people of Minnesota. And Minnesota, I want to be a transformative governor. Now is our moment to renew our commitment to the common good. I’m asking you to look up to the North Star and to see that there is a better future before us. To pursue good, we must believe that good will prevail. I know I do -- and that’s why I’m asking you to join us. Amy

In the annals of modern political history, few tactics have proven as insidious and effective as the "[color revolution](https://substack.com/redirect/29d1b324-1051-4e57-b433-a721547c07d9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)"--a non-violent, yet profoundly disruptive strategy employed by globalist and communist actors to topple sovereign governments without the overt spectacle of tanks or invasions. Coined in reference to movements like Serbia's Bulldozer Revolution (2000), Georgia's Rose Revolution (2003), and Ukraine's Orange Revolution (2004), these operations follow a meticulously scripted playbook designed to erode national sovereignty from within. The goal is not mere regime change but the installation of puppet leaders beholden to foreign powers, such as China or the United Nations, who prioritize global agendas over their citizens' interests, while expending as little blood and treasure as possible.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9oZWFydGxhbmRqb3VybmFsLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.rx0ZnFIMagTTQJlFTJYcbh8kd6p-lNkcqRhd0Ti7TxI?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=187147143)

A color revolution unfolds in four core phases:

(1) demonizing the elected leader to alienate their supporters;
(2) flooding the nation with engineered chaos, including riots, economic sabotage, and uncontrolled immigration;
(3) weaponizing institutions like the courts, media, and big tech to amplify division and silence dissent; and
(4) crowning a compliant figurehead who sells out the country.

This is no abstract theory; it's a manual honed through repeated applications in over a dozen nations, often with U.S. taxpayer funding via agencies like USAID and NGOs tied to figures like George Soros.

What makes the American experience unique--and ultimately triumphant--is how this playbook was unleashed domestically against a sitting president, only to be decisively rejected through the ballot box.

The 2024 U.S. presidential election, resulting in Donald J. Trump's landslide victory with 312 electoral votes and the largest Republican turnout among Hispanic and Black voters in history, stands as the most peaceful counter-revolution ever recorded. No shots fired, no streets barricaded, no martial law declared--just the raw power of informed citizens reclaiming their republic.

The color revolution playbook landed on U.S. soil the moment Trump defied the establishment by winning in 2016. Phase one--demonization--began immediately with the fabricated Russia collusion hoax, peddled relentlessly by the FBI, media outlets like CNN, and Democratic operatives. This wasn't mere political mudslinging; it was a calculated smear to portray the people's choice as a traitor, eroding trust in the electoral process itself. Two sham impeachments followed, each more theatrical than the last, designed not just to hobble Trump but to intimidate future patriots from challenging the status quo.

By 2020, phase two's chaos flooded the nation. Antifa-led riots scorched cities from Portland to Kenosha, with boarded-up windows and burning precincts rebranded by CNN as "[fiery but mostly peaceful protests](https://substack.com/redirect/0c53a9e0-f6ed-4b4e-be46-af918d8cee11?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)." Economic pain was amplified through lockdowns and supply chain disruptions, while the goal remained clear: make voters associate Trump with instability, fostering a desperate yearning for "normalcy" under any alternative. The election itself became a masterclass in subversion--2 a.m. ballot dumps in swing states, [51 intelligence agents](https://substack.com/redirect/56b079a5-32ec-4d27-9713-2df4a08f0068?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) falsely labeling Hunter Biden's laptop as "Russian disinformation," and Mark Zuckerberg's $400 million [infusion into Democrat-controlled vote-counting](https://substack.com/redirect/f1c50894-71dc-4a30-b493-295a4ed078e4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) operations. These weren't anomalies; they were the chaos phase in action, aimed at stealing the mandate while gaslighting the public into acceptance.

Phase three weaponized America's own institutions against its people. From 2021 to 2025, under the installed puppet regime, the border became a sieve, admitting over 12 million illegal migrants--many military-aged men from adversarial nations like China and Venezuela. Taxpayer-funded perks like free flights, hotels, and EBT cards turned cities into tinderboxes of crime and collapse. Schools and hospitals buckled under the strain, leaving Americans feeling like strangers in their homeland. Meanwhile, 91 felony charges rained down on Trump, from Mar-a-Lago raids to gag orders and mug shots, a spectacle meant to break not just one man but the spirit of resistance. Big Tech censored dissent, universities indoctrinated youth, and the media framed every pushback as "extremism." The objective? Normalize the sellout to global interests, with policies funneling billions to Ukraine's endless war while domestic priorities crumbled.
This wasn't organic discontent; it mirrored the Soros-funded upheavals in Ukraine and the Arab Spring. The same networks--BLM riot financiers, coup architects--embedded in the FBI, CIA, and corporate boardrooms orchestrated it all. By 2024, the playbook had nearly succeeded: division deepened, sovereignty eroded, and the republic teetered on the brink of irreversible transformation into a vassal state.

Yet, on November 5, 2024, the American people stared this Marxist coup dead in the eye and declared, "Not today." [Trump's victory](https://substack.com/redirect/092ae64e-73b0-40b3-9210-ad53bee6e28a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) wasn't a fluke; it was the greatest peaceful counter-revolution in history--a bloodless uprising executed through the very democratic mechanisms the globalists sought to pervert. With 312 electoral votes, a popular vote landslide, and unprecedented minority support (the biggest Hispanic and Black Republican turnout ever), voters rejected the chaos en masse. This wasn't the storming of barricades or guerrilla warfare; it was millions queuing at polls, casting ballots, and watching returns with vigilant hope. No widespread violence erupted, no militias mobilized, no constitutional crises ignited. Instead, the revolution was counted in chads, not casualties.

Why label it the most peaceful? Historical counter-revolutions pale in comparison. The American Revolution of 1776 spilled rivers of blood over eight years. France's 1830 July Revolution toppled a monarchy amid street fighting and over 800 deaths. Even the Velvet Revolution in Czechoslovakia (1989), often hailed as non-violent, involved mass strikes and protests that paralyzed the nation for weeks, with underlying tensions risking escalation. The Color Revolutions themselves, while "non-violent" on the surface, bred lasting instability--Ukraine's Orange wave led to civil war by 2014.

In contrast, America's 2024 reclamation unfolded entirely within the electoral framework. Turnout soared, with independents and disaffected Democrats crossing lines in droves, drawn by promises of secure borders, drained swamps, and restored prosperity. It was a referendum on the playbook itself--voters recognized the "sudden experts" scripting crises two weeks before elections, the "mostly peaceful" riots, and the open-border flood as foreign meddling. Their response? Overwhelming affirmation of sovereignty, achieved without a single shot fired or law bent.

This peacefulness amplified its power. By engaging the system rather than dismantling it, patriots exposed the globalists' hypocrisy: those decrying "threats to democracy" were routed by democracy's purest expression. The landslide margins--sweeping swing states and flipping demographics--sent a global message: engineered subversion crumbles against unified will.
The counter-revolution's triumph is profound, but the war rages on. The "snakes" funding BLM, Ukraine's coup, and Arab Spring still lurk in intelligence agencies, Big Tech, and academia. Midterms in 2026 and 2028 loom as potential flashpoints, where recycled scripts--[new riots](https://substack.com/redirect/c2845505-c6e4-48bf-9609-d63107df58bd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), manufactured scandals--could resurface. Yet, this victory equips America with invaluable tools: awareness of the playbook, a mandate for mass deportations, and a president committed to "all necessary measures" to reclaim the republic.

To sustain it, citizens must educate relentlessly. Teach children that communism didn't perish in 1991; it just "[dyed its hair purple and moved to Washington](https://substack.com/redirect/87ac1e4a-4a44-40c3-8d64-f46b69f70cec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)." Support fighters swinging the axe on the swamp, from border closures to institutional reforms. Recognize patterns: a "crisis" pre-election? A chorus of identical talking points? That's the color revolution playbook, live on American soil.

In staring down this threat and prevailing peacefully, 2024 redefined resilience. It proved that the brave patriots do not bow to engineered division; they vote, they organize, they endure. One closed border, one drained swamp, one restored republic at a time, America reasserts its exceptionalism. God bless the patriots who made it so--and God bless the United States of America.

"A Republic, if you can keep it." _Benjamin Franklin_

# Green energy turbine dismembers Bald Eagle in Minnesota
A University of Minnesota **[wind turbine, funded by an Obama-era green energy grant,](https://substack.com/redirect/5db62f36-0981-42c8-a9f2-9db5a2e15458?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/5db62f36-0981-42c8-a9f2-9db5a2e15458?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)struck and gruesomely killed a bald eagle--America's national symbol--in Dakota County, Minnesota. Federal officials cited the facility for violating the Bald and Golden Eagle Protection Act, proposing a $14,536 civil penalty amid renewed enforcement under the Trump administration.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5db62f36-0981-42c8-a9f2-9db5a2e15458?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Gruesome Discovery Details:** Technicians first found the eagle's lower torso and tail at the Eolos Wind Energy Research Field Station; its head and wings were located over a month later, revealing a dismembered, bloodied carcass from blade impact.
* **Federal Enforcement Action:** The Department of the Interior issued a violation notice for lacking an incidental take permit, with spokesman Matthew Middleton calling bald eagles a "national treasure" not to be collateral damage in costly wind experiments.
* **Symbolic Trump Vindication:** The incident dramatically echoes President Trump's long-standing warnings about wind turbines killing birds, as the administration pledges no more free passes for the industry while prioritizing eagle protection and affordable energy.

# Senate probes Mamdani antisemitism rollback threatens billions
Republican Sen. Bill Cassidy launched a Senate investigation into New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani on February 5, 2026, over his decision to **[rescind executive orders combating antisemitism](https://substack.com/redirect/47ac8a9c-3c67-46be-81ed-2d0bd7e677bd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and BDS participation, warning the moves could jeopardize $2.2 billion in federal education funding for the city's schools amid rising concerns for Jewish students' safety.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/47ac8a9c-3c67-46be-81ed-2d0bd7e677bd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Cassidy Demands Compliance** Cassidy's letter questions whether Mamdani's revocation of the IHRA antisemitism definition and anti-BDS order aligns with federal civil rights laws, potentially hindering Title VI enforcement in schools.
* **Funding Hangs In Balance** New York City Department of Education's $2.2 billion federal allocation as of June 2025 remains contingent on adherence to protections against discrimination, with Cassidy stressing continued eligibility depends on compliance.
* **Broader Jewish Safety Fears** The probe highlights risks to New York City's large Jewish population (1.77 million residents) and students, as Cassidy argues the actions embolden antisemitism during a surge in related incidents.

* * *
# Neighbor spotted mystery van before Guthrie mom vanished
Nancy Guthrie, 84-year-old mother of Today host Savannah Guthrie, was abducted from her Tucson home in the early hours of Sunday, authorities believe. Blood matching her DNA was found on the porch, her doorbell camera was disabled, and a **[neighbor reported seeing a suspicious unmarked white van](https://substack.com/redirect/41823e91-a9f4-48e2-b982-ffa7924a8aca?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** parked nearby days earlier. The search continues with FBI involvement and a $50,000 reward.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/41823e91-a9f4-48e2-b982-ffa7924a8aca?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Mysterious white van** spotted by neighbor Brett McIntire days before the incident, described as full-sized and unmarked with no company branding, prompting him to alert police.
* **Neighbor 's heightened fear** led Brett and his wife to consider new security cameras and carry notes for suspicious activity after the shocking event disrupted their quiet neighborhood.
* **Ongoing investigation details** include no identified suspects after six days, family pleas for proof of life amid fake ransom claims, and officials hoping she remains alive despite blood evidence.

name: David Hogg
subject: These Democrats thanked ICE
body:
You can’t make this up.
#
Hi,
Last summer, Democratic Reps. Shri Thanedar, Steve Cohen, and Stephen Lynch all voted for a resolution in Congress to “express gratitude” for ICE. While they were voting to thank ICE, Trump was actively deploying the US military to Los Angeles to crush peaceful anti-ICE protests. These are our Democratic lawmakers in action!
That’s why Leaders We Deserve is proud to support Democratic primary challengers in each of these districts and usher in a new wave of Democrats who don’t fold when it matters most. We can’t keep electing Democrats who are _this_ out of touch. We need young bold leaders like **Donavan McKinney, Justin J. Pearson** , and **Patrick Roath** who are the best of what the next generation has to offer — not more of the status quo.
ICE is terrorizing our communities. And we need Democrats who are actively fighting back.
That's why this cycle we’re challenging Democrats who have truly failed to meet this moment and are in safe congressional seats that in no way risk us losing the House. Our party cannot be seen as complicit in the invasion of our communities by masked federal agents who are there purely to terrorize communities and be Trump's paramilitary force. Our party cannot just stand by and applaud communities standing up to ICE while the Democratic Members of Congress with the real power to make change do little to nothing to stop ICE and even make it a priority to thank ICE.
If you are tired of having a party that says it can’t do anything because it’s in the minority and then miraculously still claims it can't do anything because of Republicans even when we have all three branches of government, now is the time to join us in this movement and build a party that actually fights back.
**[Make a $5 contribution now to support Leaders We Deserve. We deserve better Democrats — so we’re electing them.](https://act.leftnet.org/go/21450?c0=leftnet_em20260206.KFIF4N&refcode=em20260206-1501&amount=5&t=1&akid=1501%2E2118727%2ETi88HQ)**

Thank you,
David Hogg

body:

Tell Congress:
Protect Voting Rights, Reject the SAVE Act 2.0!

Republicans are trying to pass a new version of the anti-voter SAVE Act— their latest attack on our voting rights. This “SAVE Act 2.0” would be the
biggest legislative rollback of voting rights in our country’s history,
particularly burdening 146 million Americans who don’t have a passport, millions
who can’t easily access a birth certificate, rural voters, voters of color,
voters with disabilities, survivors of climate disasters, and the tens of
millions of people who have changed their names.

Tell Congress: keep elections free and fair — stop the SAVE Act 2.0! https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/k_ ADD YOUR NAME https://links.messages.lcv. Peter, Every eligible voter, no matter their race, income, ability, or zip code, has
the right to choose their own leaders through free and fair elections.
Generations of civil rights activists put their lives on the line to gain these
rights, but now Republicans in Congress are trying to rip them away. If passed, the SAVE Act 2.0 would deny the fundamental rights of millions of
voters across the country, roll back mail voting, cause legitimate voters’
ballots to be thrown out, and make voter registration harder for over 100
million eligible voters. We can’t let this happen. Tell Congress: reject the SAVE Act 2.0 and protect free and fair elections! https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/rNykfEgvD~ This bill would hurt communities across the country — including those already
suffering from exposure to toxic pollution and other environmental injustices —
and particularly burden 146 million Americans who don’t have a passport,
millions who can’t easily access a birth certificate, rural voters, voters of
color, voters with disabilities, survivors of climate disasters, and the tens of
millions of people who have changed their names. Collective grassroots pressure from LCV members like you is essential. Together,

Our pre-primary fundraising deadline is February 21, and what we raise before then will shape what this campaign can do in the final stretch before the March 3rd primary. We just wanted to remind, Peter to... With Tax Day approaching we here at Team Lawler wanted to make sure you remind your tax advisor of a few things. **_1) SALT Deduction_**
Rep. Lawler secured a $40,000 SALT deduction, giving New Yorkers real relief from the crushing tax burdens in our communities. This is one of the biggest wins for middle class families in decades.
**_2) Child Tax Credit_**
Families will see expanded Child Tax Credits, putting more money back into the pockets of parents trying to keep up with the cost of groceries, daycare, and basic household expenses.
**_3) No Federal Tax on Tips or Overtime_**
Workers keep more of what they earn. Service workers and hourly employees will see a meaningful boost in take-home pay from their tips and overtime pay.
**_4) Small Business Deductions Protected_**
Rep. Lawler preserved key federal tax breaks for small businesses, including pass-through income deductions and expanded expensing rules — helping local businesses grow, hire, and stay competitive.
**_5) Senior Tax Relief_**
The bill included a new **$6,000** tax deduction for seniors, helping those on fixed incomes keep more of what they’ve earned throughout their lives. **_6) Standard Deduction Doubled & Tax Rates Lowered_**
By preventing the expiration of key provisions of the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, Rep. Lawler helped double the standard deduction and keep income tax rates lower, saving taxpayers thousands as we head into Tax Day.

I didn’t run for Senate to sit on the sidelines. I’m a mom, a conservative, and proud to stand for every corner of Alabama—our cities, small towns, and rural communities alike. **I’m rooted in faith, built on family, and committed to making Alabama stronger and better for generations to come.** Alabama is a place of hard work, strong values, and unyielding independence. But the Left is trying to tear that all down. I didn’t come to Washington to play games. I came to fight for every Alabamian who feels forgotten and left behind. Whether it’s securing our borders, protecting our children, or defending our way of life, I’m here fighting for Alabama’s future. **This fight isn’t easy, but it's worth it. And I’m not going anywhere.** Will you stand with me?

Peter, It's Becca. **I’m going to be honest with you — this was a hard week on the House floor.** Hard because of what I needed to say. Hard because of what I had to witness. Hard because none of this had to happen — and yet here we are. I rose to give two speeches that I wish I never had to give. Speeches about cruelty dressed up as policy. About fear being used as a governing strategy. About people, yes, real people, being harmed by their own government. **I took that anger — that heartbreak — to the House floor and didn’t hold back.** This isn’t about catching violent criminals. It’s about power. It’s about control. And it’s about cruelty. [_**We are living in a moment that is asking something of all of us. Asking us to pay attention. Asking us to speak up. Asking us not to look away when people are being hurt. If you’re in a place to do so, will you click here and pitch in today to help me meet this moment head-on?**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124883446/600005805/237042327?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM0MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzNzMxZjAwZS1iNDAzLWYxMTEtODMyZi0wMDBkM2ExZjBlNGMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=1dv6wBHQ_M-ts9kWq5_b8_tifp0YlxZqw-cKkS9F218=) _I’ve spent time in Chicago. Minneapolis. Saint Paul. I’ve sat with families, organizers, faith leaders — folks who are scared but still brave enough to put their names and faces out there. People who knew this escalation was coming because they’ve been living with the rhetoric for years._ When you demonize and dehumanize immigrants and refugees long enough, it doesn’t stay theoretical. It turns into policy. It turns into raids. Detentions. Deaths in custody. **And now we have Americans being detained and even killed in broad daylight.** People of color afraid to leave their homes because ICE and Border Patrol are sweeping up anyone they think can help meet a quota. Based on skin color. Based on an accent. **This didn’t have to go like this. It didn’t.** **[MEET THIS MOMENT WITH ME](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124883448/600005806/237042327?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM0MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzNzMxZjAwZS1iNDAzLWYxMTEtODMyZi0wMDBkM2ExZjBlNGMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=1dv6wBHQ_M-ts9kWq5_b8_tifp0YlxZqw-cKkS9F218=)** **And then there’s Aliya. ** What happened to Aliya Rahman is chilling and it should be a warning to all of us. She is a U.S. citizen. A young software engineer. Disabled. Autistic. Living with a traumatic brain injury. She was on her way to a doctor’s appointment when ICE stopped her. They screamed conflicting orders. Dragged her from her car. She was crying out, “ _I’m disabled._ ” Begging them to understand. She was denied medical care. She lost consciousness in detention. Suffered a concussion and left in an ambulance. **I said it on the floor and I’ll say it again here: This is not about immigration enforcement. This is not about public safety.** Aliya was terrorized by her own government. And she’s not the only one. But I need you to know this. I will not stop demanding accountability. Not for Aliya. Not for the families living in fear. Not for the Americans being swept up in this dragnet. Not for anyone. But moments like this require more than speeches. They require pressure. They require organizing. They require people — like you — deciding this is the moment to step in. [_**So, I’m asking today: will you click here and make a donation today to help me keep fighting with everything I’ve got? Whether that means traveling across state lines to defend our neighbors or taking to the house floor. I’m with you in this.**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/124883450/600005807/237042327?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM0MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIzNzMxZjAwZS1iNDAzLWYxMTEtODMyZi0wMDBkM2ExZjBlNGMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=1dv6wBHQ_M-ts9kWq5_b8_tifp0YlxZqw-cKkS9F218=) Look, I know folks are tired. Tired of the outrage cycle. Tired of feeling like the system won’t listen. Tired of wondering if anything we do actually matters. **I feel that too sometimes. We’re human. But then I meet people back home. I hear their stories. I see their courage — quiet courage, everyday courage — and I’m reminded why this work matters so much.** Because the measure of our country isn’t how we treat the powerful. It’s how we treat the vulnerable. The disabled woman on her way to a doctor’s appointment. The family afraid to leave their home. The neighbor wondering if they’re next. **Moments like this test us. Test our courage. Test our compassion. I’m all in. clean_body: And it should chill all of us | = Peter, It's Becca. I’m going to be honest with you — this was a hard week on the House floor. Hard because of what I needed to say. Hard because of what I had to witness. Hard because none of this had to happen — and yet here we are. I rose to give two speeches that I wish I never had to give. Speeches about cruelty dressed up as policy. About fear being used as a governing strategy. About people, yes, real people, being harmed by their own government. I took that anger — that heartbreak — to the House floor and didn’t hold back. This isn’t about catching violent criminals. It’s about power. It’s about control. And it’s about cruelty. = I’ve spent time in Chicago. Minneapolis. Saint Paul. I’ve sat with families, organizers, faith leaders — folks who are scared but still brave enough to put their names and faces out there. People who knew this escalation was coming because they’ve been living with the rhetoric for years. When you demonize and dehumanize immigrants and refugees long enough, it doesn’t stay theoretical. It turns into policy. It turns into raids. Detentions. Deaths in custody. And now we have Americans being detained and even killed in broad daylight. People of color afraid to leave their homes because ICE and Border Patrol are sweeping up anyone they think can help meet a quota. Based on skin color. Based on an accent. This didn’t have to go like this. It didn’t. = And then there’s Aliya. What happened to Aliya Rahman is chilling and it should be a warning to all of us. She is a U.S. citizen. A young software engineer. Disabled. Autistic. Living with a traumatic brain injury. She was on her way to a doctor’s appointment when ICE stopped her. They screamed conflicting orders. Dragged her from her car. She was crying out, “ I’m disabled. ” Begging them to understand. She was denied medical care. She lost consciousness in detention. Suffered a concussion and left in an ambulance. I said it on the floor and I’ll say it again here: This is not about immigration enforcement. This is not about public safety. Aliya was terrorized by her own government. And she’s not the only one. But I need you to know this. I will not stop demanding accountability. Not for Aliya. Not for the families living in fear. Not for the Americans being swept up in this dragnet. Not for anyone. But moments like this require more than speeches. They require pressure. They require organizing. They require people — like you — deciding this is the moment to step in. = Look, I know folks are tired. Tired of the outrage cycle. Tired of feeling like the system won’t listen. Tired of wondering if anything we do actually matters. I feel that too sometimes. We’re human. But then I meet people back home. I hear their stories. I see their courage — quiet courage, everyday courage — and I’m reminded why this work matters so much. Because the measure of our country isn’t how we treat the powerful. It’s how we treat the vulnerable. The disabled woman on her way to a doctor’s appointment. The family afraid to leave their home. The neighbor wondering if they’re next. Moments like this test us. Test our courage. Test our compassion. I’m all in. I hope you are too. district, AIPAC and its network of super PACs’ candidate lost...badly.

The pro-Israel lobby group hoped that in a more purple district, voters

megadonors — but as always, they are deeply out of step with the
Democratic electorate.

That’s exactly why they have to spend millions of dollars in elections to
elect their candidates, because their policies and politicians are not
actually popular.

This is a clear rejection of AIPAC by Democratic voters — the group’s
spending and support for candidates is becoming a kiss of death in
primaries because of the work our movement has done to expose them.

Now, we can be sure that AIPAC spending this cycle will be done through

| | **Friend,** I need to say something plainly, because too much of Democratic politics right now is built on **manipulation** , and people are fed up. If you are on Democratic email lists, including from some of **my own primary opponents** , you have probably noticed the same pattern over and over again. Fake urgency.
Bogus matching claims.
Manufactured deadlines.
Emails designed to scare you, guilt you, or trick you into donating. Those emails are not an accident. They are written by **corporate political consulting firms** that treat grassroots donors like data points and revenue streams instead of people. I am running to take **Lauren Boebert’s seat** because Washington is broken. And if we are serious about fixing it, then we have to stop copying the same dishonest playbook that broke it in the first place. That is why I am doing this campaign differently. **There is no fake match in this email.**
**There is no made up deadline tonight.**
**There is no consultant pushing me to manipulate you into donating.** If you decide to contribute, it is because you believe in this movement. Not because someone lied to you. Here is something that needs to be said out loud. **If a campaign is willing to mislead you to get your money, they will mislead you once they have power.** I will not do that. I am a working class dad. An engineer. Someone who has lived paycheck to paycheck and knows exactly what it feels like to be stretched thin in an economy that keeps asking more while giving less. Integrity is not a slogan to me. It is a line I do not cross. That means something very specific in this campaign. **No corporate cash.**
**No dark money.**
**No outsourcing our fundraising to unethical consulting firms.**
**No selling donor data.**
**No abusing your inbox or your privacy.** Protecting donor information matters. Respecting your privacy matters. Treating supporters with dignity matters. And yes, it is harder to run a campaign this way. But it is necessary. Because if we want a Congress that tells the truth, we need campaigns that tell the truth first. Now let me be just as clear about **how your donation is used** , because transparency matters. When you contribute to this campaign, your money helps us: • **Pay and feed our campaign staff** , the working people putting in long hours to organize, knock doors, and talk to voters
• **Send more letters and mail pieces** directly to voters across this district
• **Film and produce our next campaign ad** , so we can tell our story without corporate filters
• **Rent a small campaign headquarters** , a real home base for organizing and community outreach
• **Reach every single voter** , by door, by mail, and beyond, so no community is ignored Every dollar goes toward real organizing, real voter contact, and building a working class campaign strong enough to defeat Lauren Boebert and replace chaos with accountability. If you are able to chip in today, thank you.
If you are not, I am still grateful you are here. **This movement is built on trust.**
**This campaign is built on integrity.**

They are written by corporate political consulting firms that treat grassroots donors like data points and revenue streams instead of people. I am running to take Lauren Boebert’s seat because Washington is broken. And if we are serious about fixing it, then we have to stop copying the same dishonest playbook that broke it in the first place. That is why I am doing this campaign differently. There is no fake match in this email. There is no made up deadline tonight. There is no consultant pushing me to manipulate you into donating. If you decide to contribute, it is because you believe in this movement. Not because someone lied to you. Here is something that needs to be said out loud. If a campaign is willing to mislead you to get your money, they will mislead you once they have power. I will not do that. I am a working class dad. An engineer. Someone who has lived paycheck to paycheck and knows exactly what it feels like to be stretched thin in an economy that keeps asking more while giving less. Integrity is not a slogan to me. It is a line I do not cross. That means something very specific in this campaign. No corporate cash. No dark money. No outsourcing our fundraising to unethical consulting firms. No selling donor data. No abusing your inbox or your privacy. Protecting donor information matters. Respecting your privacy matters. Treating supporters with dignity matters. And yes, it is harder to run a campaign this way. But it is necessary. Because if we want a Congress that tells the truth, we need campaigns that tell the truth first. Now let me be just as clear about how your donation is used , because transparency matters. When you contribute to this campaign, your money helps us: • Pay and feed our campaign staff , the working people putting in long hours to organize, knock doors, and talk to voters • Send more letters and mail pieces directly to voters across this district • Film and produce our next campaign ad , so we can tell our story without corporate filters • Rent a small campaign headquarters , a real home base for organizing and community outreach • Reach every single voter , by door, by mail, and beyond, so no community is ignored Every dollar goes toward real organizing, real voter contact, and building a working class campaign strong enough to defeat Lauren Boebert and replace chaos with accountability. If you are able to chip in today, thank you. If you are not, I am still grateful you are here. This movement is built on trust. This campaign is built on integrity. And in Washington, I will govern the same way. ****~ If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | | ---|--- | ---|--- | ~~ ---|--- We have listened to your feedback. Your personal information is protected and will never be shared. If you are interested in sending checks: Padora For Colorado PO Box 116 Severance, CO 80546 Let us show that a grassroots movement built on honesty, lived experience and working-class values can rise above fear, division and the politics of the powerful. Hi there, serving in the United States Army was one of the greatest honors of my life. I’ve never forgotten the creed I lived by when I served as an Army Ranger:

“My country expects me to move further, faster, and fight harder than any other.”
“I will shoulder more than my share of the task, whatever it may be, 100% and then some.”
“Under no circumstances will I ever embarrass my country.”

My service taught me a lot about respect, working under pressure, and the value of selfless service to others.

As a leader, it was on me to set an example — to be the last one to eat, the first one to jump out of the plane, and model the behavior I expected from others.

Right now, our president is the antithesis of this creed. He’s called for members of Congress — including me — to be imprisoned and killed, all for speaking out about his extremism.

He’s weaponizing the FBI against me, launching bogus federal inquiries against those who are putting the oaths we swore to the Constitution over the whims of this president.

I signed up to serve to protect our rights and freedoms. I ran for office to make a difference in people’s lives. Now more than ever, it’s clear: we need more leaders who are ready to do the hard work to defend the rule of law against all odds.

Thanks to these programs and support from our community in Peoria, we ultimately made it to the middle class. And I stand before you today as a member of Congress and candidate for Senate.
